articleTitle: Improving the Quality of Services and Increasing Customer Satisfaction in the Hotel
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In the competitive landscape of the hospitality industry, enhancing service quality and customer satisfaction is crucial for success. This research explores innovative methodologies and frameworks aimed at improving guest experiences through the application of advanced technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (lo'T). By analyzing customer feedback and service quality metrics, hotels can identify areas for improvement and implement strategies that foster brand loyalty.

articleTitle: Toward AI-Driven Solutions for Smart Cities in KSA
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence in the development of smart cities is considered a bedrock toward better quality of life and urban innovation. In the context of Saudi Arabia smart cities, Neom initiative aims at creating AI-enhanced urban systems that improve infrastructure, resource management, and the overall quality of life. Key use cases such as healthcare, transportation and sustainability are particularly of high emphasis in the smart cities' development. This paper explores the development of smart cities, focusing on Neom and Riyadh in Saudi Arabia. It examines the challenges faced by these cities in their journey towards smart urban development and highlights the role of artificial intelligence in addressing the different challenges. Finally, the paper provides a roadmap to successfully implement AI-based solutions in Saudi smart cities for a sustainable and smart urban development.

articleTitle: Smart Visual Pollution Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: As Saudi Arabia moves forward with its Vision 2030 initiative to improve the quality of life and services for its people, visual pollution continues to have a negative impact on the environment. However, assessing and addressing visual pollution in cities remains a challenging task due to its subjective nature and complexity. One of the main challenges is the lack of powerful and reliable intelligent systems for detecting visual pollution. To tackle this issue, we have invested our efforts in developing a cost-effective intelligent system using advanced technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT) and computer vision. This system will help detect and monitor visual pollution, including items such as water cans, paper, and plastic cups. Our smart system uses sensors like cameras to collect data and then analyzes it to display the information on a user-friendly control panel for administrators to monitor the area under study. The system has been successfully tested under various scenarios and has shown promising accuracy rates, reaching up to 87% in detecting recyclable materials. We believe that there are numerous opportunities to further enhance the performance of future designs.

articleTitle: Hausa Handwriting Character Recognition Using CNN and Tesseract
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The Hausa language, spoken by over 64 million people, is a vital part of West Africa's cultural and social fabric. Despite its importance, handwritten Hausa script recognition has little concern due to its tonal nature, unique characters, and limited datasets. This study tackles these challenges by creating a dataset and evaluating two models commonly used in handwritten recognition: a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Tesseract Optical Character Recognition (OCR). The custom CNN, trained on data from 30 volunteers with varied writing styles, achieved an accuracy of 96%, with strong precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. In contrast, Tesseract OCR struggled, particularly with Hausa-specific characters like Ɓ, Ƙ, Ƴ, and ɗ, achieving lowest accuracy for these classes. Although it had non-zero recognition in some characters, its performance was inconsistent, indicating difficulties in generalization. This work provides a scalable solution for handwritten Hausa character recognition, contributing to research on low-resource African languages and paving the way for better access to Hausa handwritten literature and integration into natural language processing applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic Safety by Strategically Placing Roadside Units for Connected Vehicles: Intercity Roads
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Connected vehicles facilitate a wide range of data exchanges, including cooperative driving, accident avoidance, real-time traffic updates, and pedestrian safety. The effectiveness of these safety measures relies heavily on communication range, as timely notifications enable drivers to make prompt decisions. This research addresses the challenge of communication range drops in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) road segments, where the range falls below essential highway safety distances, such as stopping, decision, and passing sight distances. We investigate RSU placement strategies on intercity roads, where direct field visibility scanning is both costly and complex, from a traffic safety perspective. Our study emphasizes the critical role of strategically positioned Roadside Units (RSUs) as multihop relays to extend the range and reliability of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) systems. Utilizing Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and visibility analysis through GIS software, we identify NLOS segments and optimize RSU placement to ensure sufficient communication distances for safe traffic system. The findings of this research offer a cost-effective and practical approach to improving safety and operational performance in connected vehicle ecosystems. Our results support advanced traffic safety applications, empowering engineers to predict and mitigate potential risks, thereby contributing to safer, more efficient intercity transportation systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Landmark Detection Models Through Multimodal Fusion of Visual Data and Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Detecting specific landmarks in images remains a challenging task, especially when existing traditional vision-based detection models struggle to identify the landmarks accurately. In tourism, effective landmark detection is crucial for aiding navigation and enriching cultural exploration by assisting travelers in discovering points of interest, planning trip routes, and accessing detailed historical and cultural insights. This paper introduces a multimodal approach that enhances landmark detection by combining visual and textual features extracted from images. The model utilizes a deep learning-based feature extraction technique to generate the image embedding and employs an automatic image captioning technique to extract text embeddings. These embeddings are then concatenated into a unified multimodal representation vector for each image-caption pair. By fusing visual data with corresponding captions, the proposed method improves both the accuracy and robustness of landmark identification. The proposed method has practical benefits in tourism since it supports real-time use cases as tourist route planning and culture discovery. The model is trained on a custom-built Dubai landmarks dataset and tested in live image streams from Instagram, demonstrating its potential for real-world deployment. The proposed multimodal model outperforms the visual-based model by achieving an accuracy of 91.95%.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Industrial Machinery Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques with Vibration Data for Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Industrial machinery often operates under harsh conditions, where early de-tection of anomalies is crucial for avoiding unplanned downtime and costly repairs. This study explores the application of machine learning and deep learning techniques for anomaly detection in industrial machinery using three-axis vibration data. By utilizing data collected before and after sched-uled maintenance, three models One-Class Support Vector Machine (SVM), Isolation Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Autoencoder are trained to identify anomalies in the vibration signals. The models are trained on normal operating data and tested against a dataset containing both normal and anomalous conditions. The One-Class SVM achieved the highest anomaly detection accuracy at 99.5%, outperforming the LSTM Autoencod-er with 94.1% accuracy and the Isolation Forest with 92.9% accuracy. The results highlight the efficacy of machine learning in predictive maintenance applications, providing a robust approach to early fault detection in industrial equipment.

articleTitle: Taafi: Enhancing Addiction Recovery Through Digital Health Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Addiction remains a critical challenge in urban environments, often compounded by the stigma and barriers that discourage individuals from seeking help as well as limited access to effective recovery support. Taafi is a digital platform designed to bridge this gap by offering secure, judgment-free access to addiction recovery resources. Through user-friendly interfaces, Taafi enables seamless communication between individuals and healthcare professionals via text, voice, and video consultations. The application ensures confidentiality while supporting appointment scheduling, therapy sessions, and progress tracking. By leveraging smart city innovations, Taafi enhances accessibility to addiction treatment, empowering users on their recovery journey.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sentiment and Sarcasm in Arabic YouTube Comments Utilizing AraBERT
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The emergence of social networks has transformed how people interact, leading to the development of extensive collections of user-generated content that can be examined to gain insights into cultural, social, and linguistic trends. The Arabic language, recognized for its intricate morphological features and various dialects, presents distinctive challenges within the natural language processing domain (NLP). This research explores the intricacies involved in analyzing sentiment and sarcasm within Arabic comments on YouTube by utilizing a labeled dataset that comprises both Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) and colloquial dialects. The study emphasizes the preprocessing stage, which involves addressing missing data, eliminating duplicates, and tokenizing text. It also incorporates feature extraction through AraBERT, a pre-trained transformer model specifically designed for Arabic. By Using sophisticated machine learning techniques, this research seeks to accurately classify sentiment and sarcasm while examining the linguistic patterns that define digital discourse in Arabic. Ultimately, this study aspires to enhance the overall comprehension of how sentiment and sarcasm manifest and are interpreted in Arabic online communications, providing valuable insights into both linguistic subtleties and computational approaches in Arabic NLP.

articleTitle: 90 GHz Power Amplifier in 150nm GaAs Process
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In this research a 90 GHz Common-Source (CS) and cascode 2-stage power amplifier (PA) using a UMS 150 nm GaAs pHEMT is reported. The PA design is simulated using Advanced Design System (ADS) with Class AB and Class A deviation gain enhancement topology. Wilkinson combiner with transmission line (TL)-based broadband matching method were adopted to improve output power, linearity and bandwidth. The PA was designed to improve on currently available PA designs for 6G applications and provide a compact area and low power consumption with a variety of technologies used and a gain of 14.5 dB, an output power of 14.402 dBm, a power-added efficiency of 14.254 % and a bandwidth of 17.42 GHz over 90 GHz in a compact chip size area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1.36} \times {3.22}\ {mm2}$</tex>. On the background of emerging 6G technologies, reducing power consumption while maintaining high performance remains a significant challenge. This work addresses this challenge by achieving excellent power efficiency in a compact design, making it a promising advancement for next-generation wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Baby Suffocation Prediction System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The number of suffocation cases among babies during their sleeping is increased due to the presence of blankets and sheets. Therefore, it is crucial to have a reliable system that can monitor babies during bedtime. In order to ensure the safety of children, we have developed an AI-based comprehensive smart system that provides real-time monitoring to predict suffocation incidents as soon as possible. The proposed system offers babies protection by promoting suffocation prediction within an appropriate time frame. The system is built based on the BlazeFace detection model to monitor the baby and send notifications and sound alarms if the baby's face is covered or missing for a certain amount of time. The notification is sent through the mobile application to alert the baby's parents or caregivers if there is a suffocation case that may occur. Additionally, an audible alarm is activated to grab the attention of the child's parents or caregivers and ensure quick intervention. We conducted an experiment to assess the system's effectiveness, and the prototype shows adequate accuracy and quick response. There is still space for further development, which we suggest as future work.

articleTitle: Object Identification Using Active Acoustic Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study focuses on a novel method for object identification using active acoustic sensing. While visible light and infrared sensors are affected by the lack of light or the reflection and absorption by specific materials, active acoustic sensing overcomes these challenges by utilizing sound waves. This technique identifies objects based on the differences in frequency responses caused by variations in the object's shape, density, and material. The research aims to develop a light-independent object recognition system by incorporating bone conduction speakers and piezoelectric microphones into a robotic hand. Experiments were conducted to investigate the dependency of object orientation and position, confirming the feasibility of object estimation using machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Enabling Moving Services in Enterprise Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Recently., ICT enables new models for enterprise applications and resources such as Cloud computing. The common business applications and resources management within an enterprise compose the enterprise computing environment. The wireless and mobile infrastructure support in an enterprise computing environment for mobile applications represents the common feature of the modern enterprise computing. This work proposes a model for utilizing the role of service mobility or what is called (in this work) the “moving services”” in an intermediary layer between cloud data service providers and their clients inside an enterprise computing environment. The model enables a better service mobility coverage for an enterprise. This intermediary layer introduces a required Edge/Fog computing layer that uses the wireless infrastructure to support a better data service allocation for the mobile clients and applications. This work considers the integration between Cloud Data services and their replicas inside enterprise environment. Moreover., the infrastructure of wireless enterprise networks and the challenges of deploying this model are introduced and discussed.

articleTitle: Secure Pilgrims Assistance System Using an Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The Hajj and the Umrah are the two main pilgrimages that Muslims make to Makkah, Saudi Arabia. Umrah can be done at any time, while Hajj takes place from the 8th to the 13th of Dhul Hijjah. The Hajj is considered the largest annual assembly in the world, is obligatory for every physically and financially capable Muslim at least once. During the Hajj, pilgrims travel 15 kilometers using a variety of transportation modes. The journey begins in Mina, the world's largest tent city, which houses more than 10,000 fire-resistant tents. Every year, approximately three million Muslims from more than 183 countries participate. Thus, this research aims to develop an Augmented Reality (AR) application that assists pilgrims in recognizing important sites and rituals during the Hajj pilgrimage. Furthermore, the system improves pilgrimage planning by assisting with accommodation selection and route optimization, as well as integrating national ID and mobile verification for secure identification. Also, it offers reminder notifications in Arabic and English as well as a trip planning tool to assist pilgrims in efficiently managing their time. Additionally, a specialized dashboard assists healthcare professionals and organizations, while a streamlined interface ensures effective communication with the Adahi software. User feedback mechanisms enable data-driven improvements, resulting in better decisionmaking and overall user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Cancer Detection: An Integrated Approach Using Deep Learning and Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Skin cancer poses a significant global health challenge. Hence, enhanced techniques for accurate detection and diagnosis are demanded in the fields of dermatology. This study presents an integrated approach that combines deep learning with metaheuristic algorithms to improve skin cancer detection. First, a morphological operation for hair removal, image normalization, and data augmentation are applied as preprocessing steps to enhance input quality. Moreover, ResNet-50 architecture is utilized for feature extraction. To optimize the feature selection process, particle swarm optimization (PSO) is deployed to obtain the most relevant features for classification. The final classification is performed using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Our framework is evaluated using the PH2. Results demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency in skin cancer detection. The presented approach was found to significantly advance the field of medical image analysis.

articleTitle: YOLOv7 for Real-Time Monitoring of Heat Loss Regions in Building Envelopes Using UAV-Infrared Thermography
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Drone technology has enabled efficient city-scale data collection for detecting thermal bridges in building envelopes. These thermal bridges can cause up to 30% of energy loss and can make up to 50% of the building's envelope area leading to severe heat loss, moisture infiltration, and mold growth. Addressing thermal bridges through timely monitoring can enhance building energy performance and offer comfortable occupied conditions. This paper offers a rapid, non-invasive solution for identifying areas of heat loss to improve building energy efficiency. The study utilized real world thermal bridging data collected from six city building blocks, each block containing approximately 20 buildings. The data was collected using a DJI M600 drone equipped with a FLIR-XT2 thermal camera, capturing thermal images of building envelopes. The YOLOv7 deep learning model was used to process the collected data for automated thermal anomaly detection. The model was trained over 250 epochs using standard gradient descent algorithm. During the training process, the loss function decreased gradually. The model achieved a precision of 0.58 in detecting thermal bridges. The Drone-based approach allowed capturing images from about 20 different angles per building, enhancing detection reliability. Moreover, the model achieved a high inference speed of 41 frames per second at an image size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${640}\times {640}\ \text{pixels}$</tex>, providing a method for real-time data analysis of building façades, The results demonstrate that integrating thermal imaging with advanced deep learning techniques effectively detects thermal anomalies in buildings envelopes.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology Implementation in Telemedicine—A Case Study on Sehhaty Platform in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Blockchain technology is revulotionizing the healthcare industry, particularly telemedicine by improving security, safeguarding patient data privacy, and facilitating seamless system integration and collaboration. This research focuses on the Sehhaty Platform telemedicine model in Saudi Arabia and how blockchain technology could potentially be used to improve it. In its current state, service providers have difficulty viewing the medical record history of patients among government medical institutes, hospitals, and health centers due to the incompatibility between the systems. Patients also face problems with prescription renewal, which takes a long time. As a result, we propose using the hyperledger blockchain technology to improve telemedicine resource management, security, and information exchange and enhance the automation of prescription renewal to reduce manual intervention. The proposed framework aims to overcome existing telemedicine limitations, ensuring decentralized and secure electronic health records (EHRs) while providing patients with streamlined access to healthcare services. By integrating blockchain, this research seeks to eliminate single points of failure, improve healthcare service delivery, and establish a more resilient telemedicine system. This holds significant implications for advancing Saudi Arabia's healthcare infrastructure, positioning it as a leader in adopting innovative technologies for improved patient care and system efficiency aligning with the goals of the nation's 2030 vision.

articleTitle: Classification of Diabetes Using Ensemble and Individual Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by elevated blood glucose levels, posing significant health and economic challenges globally. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of Random Forest and Decision Tree algorithms in classifying diabetes, addressing the increasing prevalence of the disease and the necessity for accurate diagnostic tools. Both algorithms were applied to a dataset containing 100,000 entries sourced from Kaggle. The study employed systematic preprocessing steps, including normalization and feature selection, to optimize data quality. The dataset was split into training (80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and testing (20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) subsets, ensuring robust evaluation. Random Forest and Decision Tree algorithms were implemented with carefully tuned parameters to maximize performance, and their outputs were assessed using metrics such as accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity. Results revealed that Random Forest achieved a higher accuracy of 96%, outperforming Decision Tree's 95%, with superior sensitivity and specificity. These findings highlight Random Forest's effectiveness in capturing complex patterns and reducing overfitting, which is consistent with prior studies on medical data classification. This research underscores the importance of algorithm selection and data preprocessing in improving diabetes classification. Future studies should explore ensemble methods and diverse datasets to enhance generalizability and predictive accuracy, offering valuable insights for healthcare applications.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Polymorphic Malware
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Polymorphic malware have the ability to constantly change its code structure while retaining malicious functionality, making it very hard to detect due to the sophistication of evolving cyber threats. Traditional signature-based and heuristic techniques have fallen flat against such evolving threats, far more advanced strategies are required for detection. This study proposes a hybrid ensemble deep learning approach to detect polymorphic malware by combining the strengths of Deep Learning models such as Autoencoders, LSTM networks, and Gradient Boosting. In that direction, the proposed approach will enhance the accuracy of detection, reduce false positives and negatives, and offer better adaptability to changing malware behaviours. The proposed hybrid ensemble technique outperforms the results of the base models with an accuracy of 99.21 % and a value of 0.99 for the F1-score after optimal feature selection using Recursive Feature Elimination, as obtained by the EMBER dataset. This paper has demonstrated that the work of different deep learning models combined with an ensemble technique is better in finding polymorphic malware in practical cybersecurity applications.

articleTitle: Generative AI in Computer Science Education: Insights from Topic Modeling and Text Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping educational landscapes., particularly in computer science education. This study investigates research trends in generative AI applications through text network and topic modeling analyses. A comprehensive literature review across IEEE Xplore., Scopus., and Web of Science identified 151 studies published between 2023 and 2024. Text network analysis revealed that “AI.,” “student.,” “education.,” “learning.,” and “performance” were the most frequently occurring terms., highlighting key research themes. Ego-network analysis demonstrated strong interconnectivity between educational AI tools and student learning outcomes. Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)., four major research topics emerged: educational chatbots (35.1 %)., AI literacy (25.8%)., exam performance (21.8%)., and technology integration (17.2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). Findings indicate a dominant focus on chatbots for student engagement., while ethical concerns and multimodal AI applications remain underexplored. The study underscores the necessity of addressing AI literacy gaps and enhancing interdisciplinary AI integration in educational settings. Despite its potential., generative AI adoption is hindered by privacy risks., uneven technological access., and the lack of standardized policies. Future research should focus on ethical AI frameworks., multimodal AI tools., and long-term learning outcomes. This study provides a data-driven foundation for understanding the evolving role of generative AI in education and its implications for educators., policymakers., and researchers.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Travel Sequence Recommendations: A Dubai Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The emergence of tourism has brought a paradigm shift in how travel recommendations are generated. For tourists, planning an itinerary is a challenging task given the necessity to suggest a visit sequence encompassing Points of Interest (PoIs) in unfamiliar cities. The additional complexity lies in selecting PoIs that match their individual preferences and trip constraints. This paper presents a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework that integrates PoI proximity, popularity, and user interest alignment components that have usually been addressed separately in previous studies. The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), with the DRL agent utilizing a Deep Q-Network (DQN) architecture and experience replay to enhance learning efficiency. The agent interacts with the environment to generate travel sequences based on user-specified interests, trip duration, and starting time. A case study in Dubai demonstrates the framework's ability to produce optimal travel sequences that align with user preferences, maximize time efficiency, and consider the popularity of PoIs, ultimately enhancing the overall travel experience.

articleTitle: WPDS - Smart Wireless Water Pollution Detection System using IoT for Better Monitoring of Water Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Most Saudi Arabian research about marine pollution, especially water pollution, detects a lot of sources of marine contaminants including sewage discharge, traces of hydrocarbons, oil, petroleum, trace metals, residual chlorine, and other suspended particles. The Internet of Things has emerged as one of the most important technologies of the twenty-first century in interacting with devices and assisting in data collection and analysis. In this paper, an IoT-based smart wireless water pollution detection system is introduced. To validate the accuracy of this system's measurements, four different water sources were tested hourly over a 12-hour period. The results aligned with the investigation's predictions. Data on key parameters, such as the relationships between temperature, conductivity, and pH, were recorded for each sample using a proposed cloud-based application for improved monitoring of water quality. This paper highlights the effective implementation of IoT and GSM technology, which enables the end user to receive alerts based on reference values and take immediate action to maintain water quality.

articleTitle: Exploring AI Applications for Optimal Business Location Selection in Smart Cities: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: With the rapid growth of urbanization, adaptive technologies are being used to enhance infrastructure, services and the economy of smart cities. A critical aspect in smart cities' advancement is optimizing business location selection such that economic opportunities and resource efficiency are well-balanced. To identify where new endeavors might be most valuable, large scale urban data has been recognized as an important area where Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be utilized. This study reviews AI applications for finding optimal business locations in smart cities. The objective is to understand the methodologies used, factors considered and how such models can be implemented in practical business environments. The review revealed three main findings: (i) Random Forest is the most dominant machine learning algorithm used representing around 43% of the overall studies due to its robust performance while handling enormous and complicated data sets. (ii) Most papers primarily examined demographic and geographical factors with some studies incorporating sales-related and behavioral factors. (iii) The highest accuracy reported was 98.4%, achieved by the Improved Gravity Model and PCA-BP Neural Network. While many models have potential for real-world implementation, only a few studies have assessed the models in actual business scenarios. The outcomes reveal that even though accuracy obtained through AI techniques are impressive, the lack of real-world verification merits investigation. Therefore, next studies must aim at the implementation of these models to the real world to improve their applicability in smart city planning.

articleTitle: A Method for Assessing the Performance of Cryptographic Pseudorandom Number Generators Utilizing Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Cryptographic pseudorandom number generators (CPRNGs) play a crucial role in maintaining the security and trustworthiness of cryptographic frameworks. Their efficiency directly influences the robustness of encryption, authentication, and various other security mechanisms. Conventional approaches for assessing CPRNG quality typically depend on statistical randomness evaluations, which may overlook subtle patterns or vulnerabilities. This paper presents an innovative technique for evaluating CPRNG performance through the use of artificial neural networks (ANNs). By harnessing ANNs' ability to detect patterns, we propose a system that uncovers potential biases and anomalies in CPRNG outputs. This method assesses both the randomness and unpredictability of the generated sequences, thus delivering a more thorough evaluation than traditional methods. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed ANN -based assessment effectively identifies weaknesses in several commonly utilized CPRNGs, representing notable progress in cryptographic analysis. This research emphasizes the promise of machine learning methodologies in improving the reliability and security of cryptographic systems.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Paper-Based Testing Model for the TOEFL Institutional Testing Program
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study introduces an IoT-enhanced model for paper-based testing, specifically designed for the TOEFL Institutional Testing Program (ITP). The proposed model integrates Internet of Things (IoT) technology to improve the traditional paper-based testing process by enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and security. The system provides automatic test scanning, real-time data gathering, and secure cloud-based result storage. The study used a mixed-method technique. A sample of 25 respondents was chosen to assess the effectiveness of the system. Quantitative data has been collected through automated test scoring and error rate analysis, while qualitative feedback was gained through participant surveys on usability and overall experience. The results demonstrate that the IoT-based system dramatically minimizes manual errors, speeds up the grading process, and enhances the entire testing experience for both administrators and participants. This paper investigates the practical applications of IoT in language proficiency testing and proposes future developments to improve testing efficiency and security in large-scale educational evaluations.

articleTitle: Dual Band LoRa/GPS Dipole Antenna with Harmonic Suppression Capability
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This paper describes the design and testing of a compact dual-band printed dipole antenna, optimized for 916 MHz and 1.57 GHz, aimed at LoRa and GPS applications. The design features a linear dipole functioning at 916 MHz and 2.7 GHz. A small triangular-shaped linear balun has been developed as the matching network. Parasitic elements are employed to tune the second frequency to 1.57 GHz through a parametric study. Meanwhile, a stub is used to suppress the undesired 2.7 GHz frequency. This antenna is capable of operating on dual-frequency bands simultaneously with high efficiency in suppressing the unwanted frequency. The antenna exhibits a return loss of -20 dB at 916 MHz and -11 dB at 1.57 GHz, with VSWR values of 1.31 and 1.98, respectively. The gain is 2.05 dBi at 916 MHz and 1.05 dBi at 1.57 GHz. The bandwidth for the band is 78 MHz, while the bandwidth for the GPS band is 24 MHz, respectively. The radiation pattern of the antenna exhibits a focused E-plane and a circularly polarized H-plane at both frequencies. Due to its compact design and dual-band functionality, this antenna holds significant promise for IoT applications that demand both LoRa and GPS communication, especially in scenarios where a small yet efficient form factor is crucial.

articleTitle: Deep Fake Image Generation, Detection Techniques - Overcoming Challenges of Deep Fake, Ethical Implications Regulation: A Risk-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The aim of this research is to identify and asses ethical risks of deepfake technology, as well as providing appropriate risk prevention, mitigation, redressal and monitoring measures. Authors then provide a design and implementation for a framework as an ethics compliance checker tool. A procedure for conducting conformity assessment of Ethical development and deployment of Deep fake Technology in line with the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) Deep fake Guidelines. Measuring the process before and after prove the improvements in decision making, increased accountability and enhanced governance.

articleTitle: No Bag Left Behind
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Unattended bags in public spaces such as airports and train stations pose significant security risks. In this paper, we propose a real-time algorithm for detecting and monitoring unattended bags that integrates advanced computer vision techniques with proximity analysis. Our al-gorithm employs a Convolutional Neural Network to identify both bags and individuals, while a proximity analysis module evaluates the spatial relationships and distances between them using a defined threshold. Designed to minimize disruptions, the algorithm reduces false positives, ensuring timely and reliable alerts for genuinely unattended bags. The proposed algorithm is rigorously tested across four real-world scenarios, demonstrating exceptional accuracy in identifying unattended bags. Furthermore, it effectively captures information about individuals who left these items behind, providing critical insights for security personnel during investigations. The code and the dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/ahmadmelebari/No-Bag-Left-Behind.hit.

articleTitle: Optimized Hardware Implementation of FOC for BLDCs in UAVs Using a 2-DOF PI (Blended PI-IP) Controller and PSO
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) increasingly perform complex missions, such as multi-input multi-output (MIMO) cooperative control, which require precise and responsive motor torque regulation. Inadequate torque control can lead to instability and reduced accuracy, especially in challenging environments affected by air turbulence. Traditional open-loop Electronic Speed Controllers (ESCs) exhibit limitations in dynamic response, disturbance rejection, and control precision. To overcome these limitations, we implemented a hardware-based Field-Oriented Control (FOC) system using blended PI-IP regulators. This system optimizes motor performance, enhances disturbance rejection, minimizes steady-state error, and improves dynamic response for more precise control. Additionally, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was applied to fine-tune the FOC parameters. Control strategies were tested under various disturbances to evaluate their robustness. Our results show that FOC significantly outperforms traditional open-loop and closed-loop methods, particularly in stability and disturbance rejection. The PSO-optimized FOC using a 2-DOF PI regulator “Blending of PI Regulator and IP Regulator” for the speed control loop demonstrates superior dynamic response, enhanced disturbance rejection, and greater accuracy, making it a highly promising solution for advanced UAV applications.

articleTitle: Innovative Eye-Tracking and Blink Detection System for Empowering Disabled Users Through Assistive Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Individuals with physical disabilities, particularly those with speech impairments, often face significant barriers in communication due to the limitations of conventional methods. To address this challenge, the Eye Communicator system offers an alternative by leveraging eye detection and eye aspect ratio (EAR) analysis to capture and interpret eye blinks. This allows users to interact with a virtual interface, selecting letters, words, or commands, which are then converted into speech. The system achieves high accuracy rates of 98.89% for icon selection and 99.41% for text input, ensuring efficient and reliable communication. Moreover, the Eye Communicator includes Arabic language support, a feature rarely found in existing eye-gaze systems, making it accessible to Arabic-speaking users. Designed for use in both healthcare and educational settings, the system provides a cost-effective and user-friendly solution that enhances inclusivity and fosters independence for individuals with disabilities.

articleTitle: A Simultaneous Confusion-Diffusion Structure for Fast Image Encryption Based on Plaintext-Related Mechanism and Dynamic Josephus Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The security of image cryptosystem is fundamentally contingent upon the efficacy of the confusion and diffusion methodologies employed by the cryptosystem, as well as the dynamic behavior of chaotic systems. Nonetheless, prevailing chaos-based image cryptosystem are hindered by slow performance, inadequate resistance to a variety of attacks, a lack of correlation between the input image and the encryption key, suboptimal dynamic performance, and limited sensitivity to chaotic systems. In order to mitigate these deficiencies, this paper presents a simultaneous confusion-diffusion structure for image encryption based on a plaintext-related mechanism, which demonstrates a high correlation with the plain image using the U-Quark hash function and Collatz conjecture. Firstly, the plain image is divided into non-overlapping blocks. Secondly, the dynamic Josephus trajectory permutes the image blocks using random indices generated through a 7D hyperchaotic system. Thirdly, a parallel simultaneous confusion-diffusion structure is employed to confuse and diffuse all image pixels. The results of the experimental study imply that the recommended cryptographic approach, in relation to earlier investigations, delivers a variety of benefits concerning MSE, PSNR, entropy and correlation coefficient indicators, accomplishing an encryption time of around 0.024 seconds and a key size greater than about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">266</sup>. Furthermore, it exhibits commendable resilience against a spectrum of attacks.

articleTitle: Design of innovative Stand-alone Hybrid Renewable Generation System Harnessing Air Condition Wastes
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The increasing need for energy, especially in countries with hot climates such as Saudi Arabia, where air conditioning (AC) units are frequently used, highlights the urgent need for renewable energy solutions to reduce dependence on fossil fuels for electricity generation. In response, this paper presents a novel design for an Environmental Hybrid Power Generation System (EH-PGS) that aims to alleviate rising electricity costs while supporting the utilization of renewable energy. The EH-PGS harnesses waste from AC units to generate electricity by employing renewable energy resources within the AC's outdoor unit. The main renewable energy sources utilized in this study are solar panel, wind turbines, and Thermoelectric Generators (TEGs). This innovative approach captures sunlight, harnesses wasted airflow, and utilizes surplus heat from the AC, maximizing the potential for energy generation. A comparative analysis was conducted using MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the EH-PGS against other systems, including Stand-alone systems and Hybrid systems for the used renewable sources. This analysis assessed efficiency and energy savings while ensuring a consistent power supply. Results demonstrate the superiority of the EH-PGS in both performance and efficiency compared to alternative systems as it generates 50 W - 135 W of power in different scenarios. Following successful simulation validation, a prototype of the EH-PGS was developed, featuring a 34x20x3 cm solar panel and a three-blade vertical wind turbine with a 25 cm diameter. The prototype yielded an approximate power output of 6W. The system also includes a mobile application for real-time monitoring of power and controlling loads. This approach minimizes reliance on fossil fuels, enhances energy efficiency, and offers a sustainable solution to energy challenges in high-temperature regions.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Electric Vehicle Battery Swap Charging Station for Smart Cities in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The adoption of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in Saudi Arabia is gaining traction, necessitating the establishment of innovative charging solutions such as swap battery electric vehicle charging stations (SBEVCS). The research proposes optimal design of SBEVCS that minimizes the waiting time of charging and improves the energy mismatch in distribution network considering travel behavior in Saudi Arabia since limited research addressed that. In this work, SBEVCS has been modeled using Discrete Event Simulation (DES) that considers the uncertainty of driving behavior in Electric Vehicles (EVs) such as station arrival rates, charging energy required, and waiting time of charging. A field measurement of conventional vehicles using gasoline station is conducted in Makkah, Saudi Arabia to overcome the gap in related work, to estimate the driving behavior of vehicles in Saudi Arabia. The outcomes from this field measurement have been considered as inputs for DES modeling for SBEVCS in order to obtain the optimal design of this station in terms of number of swap battery servers, number of batteries in reserved storage, and EV charging load profile of SBEVCS to support its integration to Saudi electrical grid. The results of DES show that the arrival rates and the penetration level of EVs have the main impact on designing SBEVCS. 15 – 30 reserved batteries are required in small SBEVCS, where 40 – 60 reserved batteries are required in medium SBEVCS. In large SBEVCS at least 80 reserved batteries are required in order to guarantee the charging quality of service, so service time does not exceed 6 minutes. The outcomes of this work support the development of SBEVCS in Saudi Arabia as a crucial step towards fostering an efficient and user-friendly BEV ecosystem.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Analysis of Internet of Things (IoT) Research Trends on Electric Cars
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study focuses on analyzing articles related to the use of IoT technology in electric cars. This study aims to identify and analyze scientific literature on this topic in the past and present. This study uses a bibliometric analysis approach based on articles published in journals and conferences indexed by Scopus. Bibliometric analysis is used to analyze the number of publications, the most published articles, keyword analysis, and research trends on IoT technology in electric cars. Research trends are analyzed using VOSviewer to describe the relationship between keywords. The results show that 51 documents, consisting of 20 journal articles and 31 conference articles, were published between 2016 and 2024. Research related to the implementation of IoT in electric cars has developed every year, and an increase in the number of publications marks this. The keywords with the highest frequency on this topic include the Internet of Things, electric vehicles, charging (batteries), electric cars, and digital storage. Other topics related to the application of IoT in electric cars, such as autonomous driving and intelligent systems, provide a clear picture of research trends in this area. Other topics include supporting technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain, which increase the security and efficiency of IoT -based systems.

articleTitle: Predicting the Lifespan of Lithium-Ion Batteries: Integrating Initial Data with Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Accurate lithium-ion battery cycle life prediction from early operational data is essential for optimizing manufacturing processes, ensuring product reliability, and enabling proactive maintenance. This study presents a machine learning-based approach that predicts the remaining cycle life using features derived from the first 100 operation cycles, including discharge capacity trends, internal resistance changes, and voltage characteristics. A linear regression model with elastic net regularization was trained on data from 124 cells, with hyperparameters optimized through cross-validation. The model achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 210 cycles and an average percentage error of 9.96% on test data, demonstrating strong predictive performance for cycle lives between 500 and 1200 cycles despite underestimations for longer-lived cells due to data distribution imbalances. This work highlights the promise of data-driven methods for early-stage battery life cycle prediction, offering a scalable and interpretable framework to support advancements in battery technology and maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Metaverse Design Trends Shaping Smart Cities Through Sentiment and Influencer Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The metaverse, blending virtual and physical realities, offers transformative potential for smart cities. This paper examines emerging design trends in the metaverse by analyzing sentiments expressed on X (Twitter) and the influence of key voices on user engagement. Through sentiment analysis and influencer metrics, this study explores how themes like augmented reality (AR), virtual spaces, and NFTs in metaverse design are received, impacting smart city concepts like smart infrastructure and urban mobility. Findings highlight influencers' roles in shaping discourse, identifying themes that gain traction via hashtags. Positive sentiments surround user experience and economic potential, while concerns arise regarding technical limitations and data security. This study provides insights into how metaverse engagement might shape smart city designs, guiding future strategies.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Approach to Energy Management: Multisectoral Collaboration for Second-Life Electric Vehicle Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The primary issue in electric vehicle development is the elevated cost of batteries, a significant determinant of production expenses. Electric vehicle batteries possess a finite lifespan and become unsuitable for vehicular requirements once specific conditions are fulfilled. The battery requires replacement. These utilized batteries retain capacity and are suitable for a variety of alternative applications. This creates new market opportunities in second-life applications as a sustainable solution, particularly in the areas of energy management and integration with smart grids. Notwithstanding this potential, the relatively extended battery life means that business models for second-life applications remain in the early phase of development. Various elements affect this evolution, such as technological preparedness, legal frameworks, and market support. Enhancing the utilization of electric vehicle batteries offers sustainable commercial opportunities, requiring collaboration among diverse entities while considering the interests of every party involved and their impact on the environment and society. This study performed a literature analysis to identify essential activities, principal actors and their responsibilities, and challenges encountered in the second-life application ecosystem of electric vehicle batteries. The review's findings suggest that the effectiveness of battery reuse necessitates meticulous collaboration among battery producers, automobile firms, energy service providers, consumers, and governmental entities. The challenges encountered encompassed safety standards, economic efficiency, consumer acceptance, and regulatory support. This study's findings offer significant insights for the business sector, policymakers, and stakeholders, indicating that the establishment of an ecosystem facilitating the second life of electric vehicle batteries necessitates cross-sector collaboration and innovative business models to optimize economic and environmental benefits.

articleTitle: Quantum Cryptography and Post-Quantum Security: Safeguarding Cryptographic Protocols Against Quantum Threats
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: As quantum computing progresses towards practical realization, the security of existing cryptographic protocols, such as RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), faces unprecedented risks. Quantum algorithms like Shor's Algorithm threaten to undermine the security of these widely used encryption schemes, necessitating the development of quantum-resistant alternatives. This paper explores the vulnerabilities of current cryptographic protocols in the quantum era and investigates quantum-safe cryptographic techniques such as lattice-based, hash-based, and code-based cryptography. Additionally, we delve into Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), a method that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to securely distribute cryptographic keys, ensuring secure communication even in the presence of quantum adversaries. The integration of QKD with post-quantum cryptographic algorithms is proposed as a robust approach to future-proofing cybersecurity. The paper concludes with a discussion of practical challenges in implementing quantum-safe systems and highlights future research directions to strengthen cryptographic resilience against quantum threats.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning Integration for Enhanced Photovoltaic System Power Forecasting: A Novel Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into power distribution networks presents challenges due to the unpredictable nature of power output, which affects grid reliability and energy management. Accurate forecasting of a PV power output is therefore critical. This study proposes a novel collaborative learning intergration (CLI) stacking ensemble energy forecasting model approach, designed to forecast real-time hourly power output of a 39.02 kWp photovoltaic system using the historical real time power generation output of the system and the hourly time correlating meteorological data. Unlike conventional methods that simply average model predictions or develop a meta learner, the proposed topology allows individual machine learning models to interact and learn from each other through mutual reinforcement, thereby enhancing forecasting accuracy. The algorithm is evaluated against benchmark independent and stacked models to analyze its performance as an improved forecasting model. The experiment results show that the proposed collaborative learning integration stacked ensemble model outperforms the five benchmark models, achieving an R-square (R2), mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) accuracy of 0.89, 1.44 and 2.47 respectively. The residual analysis highlighted that the collaborative learning intergration model was more effective at minimising long-term forecast errors compared to other models. The proposed model can be highly useful for predicting the performance of small and large-scale solar PV power plants in a multi-step ahead forecasting.

articleTitle: Stacked LSTM-GRU with Double Attention model for Arabic Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The proliferation of online opinions, fueled by the rise of social media and review platforms, has underscored the significance of sentiment analysis across diverse domains, including business, marketing, and politics. Sentiment analysis, a pivotal task within natural language processing, aims to analyze and classify sentiments expressed in textual data. Recent research has increasingly concentrated on aspect-level sentiment analysis, which offers enhanced accuracy compared to document- and sentence-level approaches by effectively addressing the multi-faceted aspects and varying sentiments present in individual reviews. However, implementing aspect-based sentiment analysis in the Arabic language poses unique challenges due to its intricate morphology and dialectal variations, resulting in a relative scarcity of Arabic-specific studies. This research introduces an Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis model specifically designed for Arabic, utilizing AraBERT for word embeddings in conjunction with stacked LSTM and GRU layers to capture sequential dependencies and aspect-specific sentiments. A dual attention mechanism is employed to highlight the most pertinent words associated with the target aspect. The model's outputs are subsequently processed through a dense layer with softmax activation for sentiment classification. Experimental findings indicate that the model outperforms the performance of the state-of-the-art models, attaining an accuracy of 94.71%

articleTitle: Autonomous Parking Valet System: Path Planning and Control in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Automated parking valet systems are increasingly vital for autonomous driving, offering substantial benefits in safety, space utilization, and operational efficiency. This paper presents a comprehensive, MATLAB-based framework for autonomous parking, designed with a multi-layered occupancy grid model and integrating advanced path planning and control algorithms. Using a hybrid A* algorithm for global path planning and the Time Elastic Band (TEB) method for real-time trajectory smoothing the system achieves high precision in navigation through constrained spaces. Precise vehicle control is maintained through Stanley lateral control and a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller for longitudinal adjustments, ensuring accuracy in both forward and reverse parking maneuvers. Simulated within a controlled parking lot environment, the system demonstrates high efficiency and accuracy, meeting path smoothness and collision-avoidance requirements. Results validate its capability for complex parking scenarios, establishing a foundation for future development, including dynamic obstacle handling and real-time SLAM, for application in urban environments.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Cyber Security: Deephoax Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of deep hoaxes, such as fake news and phishing schemes, poses a significant threat to cybersecurity, undermining trust and spreading misinformation. In Indonesia, surveys indicate that more than 60% of people exposed to hoax news believe that it is true, emphasizing the urgent need for robust detection methods. Traditional cybersecurity approaches often struggle to keep pace with the growing scale and sophistication of these attacks. To address this challenge, this research investigates the use of deep learning techniques, specifically focusing on text-based hoax detection in the Indonesian language. The study fine-tunes IndoBERT, a pretrained deep learning model optimized for Indonesian text, to enhance the accuracy and scalability of hoax detection. The IndoBERT model was trained on a balanced dataset of 29,552 articles, comprising both hoax and real news content, collected from the Mafindo API and Kaggle's Indonesia News Dataset. The model was fine-tuned using supervised learning and evaluated using several key metrics, including accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall. The results demonstrate that IndoBERT outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, achieving an accuracy of 98.51%, an F1-score of 98.44%, and a precision of 98.23% on the test set. These results highlight the effectiveness of IndoBERT for hoax detection, which offers a scalable solution to improve cybersecurity defenses against deceptive content. This research contributes to the integration of advanced deep learning models into cybersecurity systems, addressing the evolving landscape of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Warehouse Management and Tracking System for University Assets Using IoT Technology to Optimize Operations and Reduce Randomness
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Efficient asset management within university environments is a crucial aspect of ensuring smooth daily operations. Universities often struggle with disorganized tracking systems for their tools, equipment, and furniture, leading to losses or delays in operations. This project aims to design a robust warehouse management and tracking system using Internet of Things (IoT) technology to optimize the management of university assets. The proposed system will allow real-time tracking, monitoring, and reporting of assets to prevent random losses and streamline the process of checking out and returning equipment. The integration of IoT devices will facilitate seamless data collection, reducing manual errors, ensuring accountability, and enhancing overall efficiency. This solution will address the core issue of disorganization in university storage and asset management, providing a sustainable and scalable system for the future.

articleTitle: S-Shaped Versus V-Shaped Transfer Functions for Salp Swarm Algorithm in Sentiment Analysis Feature Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This paper proposed an advanced method to enhance sentiment analysis (SA) for large-scale datasets. Given the complexity of SA, especially when dealing with high-dimensional data rich in features, effective feature selection (FS) becomes crucial to manage and reduce the data's dimensionality. Conventional machine learning techniques often fall short in this regard, highlighting the need for more sophisticated FS algorithms. In this study, we propose an improved bio-inspired optimization technique known as the Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) as a wrapper method for feature selection to enhance sentiment analysis of Indonesian-language tweets. Feature selection is inherently an NP-hard problem, making meta-heuristic algorithms like SSA a more efficient choice than exact methods. However, SSA typically faces challenges in terms of slow convergence, particularly in binary problems and large datasets. To address this, we introduce eight SSA variants, each employing S-shaped and V-shaped transfer functions to map the continuous search space into a discrete one, thus facilitating efficient feature selection. The proposed SSA-based approach is benchmarked against existing metaheuristic algorithms, including both Ant Lion Optimization (ALO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Comparative experiments demonstrate that the enhanced SSA method outperforms both PSO and ALO, showing superior performance in terms of classification accuracy and processing time. Specifically, the experimental results reveal that the SSA combined with the V2-shaped transfer function achieved in just 5.16 seconds using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, with an accuracy of 89.76%. Similarly, the SSA integrated with the S1-shaped transfer function closely follows, completing the processing in 4.38 seconds with an accuracy of 89.43%. These findings indicate that the proposed SSA-based feature selection approach efficiently explores the feature space, selects the most informative features, and significantly improves the classification accuracy for sentiment analysis tasks.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) using Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices in healthcare requires robust intrusion detection systems to safeguard sensitive data and ensure patient safety. This study presents a novel approach utilizing Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) architectures for intrusion detection in IoMT environments, leveraging the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 dataset. Addressing the prevalent issue of class imbalance, we compare the impact of Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), weighted loss functions, and a hybrid over- and under-sampling strategy to enhance detection accuracy. Our research implements and evaluates multiple ELM architectures, comparing their performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC). The results demonstrate that the weighted loss function method significantly improves the detection capabilities of ELMs, providing an effective solution for real-time intrusion detection in healthcare IoMT systems.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Multi-Crop Disease Detection and Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based solution for the detection and classification of crop diseases in tomato, banana, and mango leaves using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). As crop diseases significantly impact agricultural productivity, the need for early, accurate detection is crucial for ensuring food security and economic stability. The proposed model leverages large datasets from publicly available sources and employs advanced techniques such as transfer learning and data augmentation. By automating disease identification, the system reduces reliance on manual inspections and mitigates environmental harm from excessive pesticide use. The research focuses on the development and evaluation of crop-specific models, followed by the deployment of the solution on accessible platforms, including mobile devices and edge computing devices, to facilitate real-time diagnostics in resource-constrained regions. The study demonstrates the potential of AI in transforming agricultural practices by enhancing productivity and sustainability. The proposed models achieved validation accuracies of 87.80% for tomatoes, 82.66% for bananas, and 85.62% for mangoes, highlighting their effectiveness across different crops. Additionally, the solution's scalability and adaptability make it a viable tool for broader agricultural applications.

articleTitle: Accurate and Interpretable Maize Disease Classification Using Deep Transfer Learning and XAI
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study addresses the critical need for accurate and timely maize disease classification, developing a robust and interpretable system leveraging deep transfer learning and Explainable AI (XAI). Six prominent pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) were investigated: AlexNet, GoogleNet, ResNet-l0l, MobileNet-v2, VGG-19, and EfficientN et-b0. These diverse architectures were fine-tuned on a meticulously curated maize disease dataset comprising four classes: healthy leaves, common rust, gray leaf spot, and blight. The dataset was rigorously partitioned into training (70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), validation (15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), and testing (15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) sets. Fine-tuning proved highly effective across all architectures. VGG-19 achieved the highest test accuracy at 96.7%, followed closely by MobileNet-v2 (96.5%) and ResNet-l0l (95.9%). GoogleNet also demonstrated strong performance with a test accuracy of 95.5%, while EfficientNet-b0 and AlexNet achieved 94.3% and 93.6% respectively. All models exhibited near-perfect accuracy on healthy leaves; however, performance varied across disease classes. To enhance transparency and trust, explainable AI (XAI) methods-specifically LIME, Grad-CAM, and Occlusion Sensitivity-were employed to interpret the decision-making process of the top-performing VGG-19 model. These methods visualized the image regions most influential for classification, confirming the model's focus on relevant disease features rather than spurious correlations. This research demonstrates that combining deep transfer learning with explainable AI (XAI) can create highly accurate and interpretable diagnostic tools to support sustainable agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Forecasting Prices of Strategic Food Products: Time Series Models in the Context of Post-Crisis Market Disruption
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In a post-crisis context, anticipating variations in raw material prices is essential for smart cities. At the beginning of this decade, two major global crises disrupted various market sectors: the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russian-Ukrainian war. Wheat is an essential product that contributes to food security in many countries. The price of this cereal fluctuated considerably during the two crises. Russia and Ukraine account for up to 28% of the wheat export market. Today, the wheat market seems to be gradually stabilizing from these disturbances. This paper explores reliable forecasting models to estimate wheat prices and support decision-making in the post-crisis period. To this end, two time-series forecasting techniques are compared: the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model (ARIMA), known for its reliability in financial forecasting, and the Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM). The results reveal that the LSTM model achieves an accuracy of 97.49%, outperforming the ARIMA model, which registers an accuracy of 77%. These results underline the effectiveness of deep learning models for forecasting during periods of high price volatility, compared with conventional models.

articleTitle: Smart Attendance Management System in Student Housing: A Case Study at King Abdulaziz University
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Student housing is adapting to the demands of modern education, and ensuring safety is vital, alongside addressing legal, ethical, and parental concerns. Effective access control policies are essential; however, manual tracking of entrances and exits often leads to unauthorized access and inefficiencies. This paper describes the design and implementation of a Smart Attendance Management System (SAMS) in the dormitories of King Abdulaziz University, utilizing a fingerprint-based access system where each student is registered in a biometric database for secure entry. This system not only ensures that only authorized individuals can enter the facility but also automates attendance procedures, eliminating traditional paper-based processes that are often tedious and error-prone. The system tracks student movement in real-time, with administrators receiving instant alerts for any unusual delays. Additionally, the system enhances communication and safety by sending SMS notifications to students and security personnel regarding entry and exit times. Our research aims to analyze entry and exit patterns to address existing security weaknesses and enhance the safety of student housing.

articleTitle: IntelliGuard: An AI-Powered Threat Detection System for Smart Home Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The growing application of smart home technologies has exposed significant vulnerabilities in cybersecurity. This research proposes a lightweight, AI-powered Threat Detection System (TDS) aimed at improving the security of IoT devices in smart homes by combining Azure Cloud and Google Big-Query for efficient data storage and processing. The proposed system implements firewalls and Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption to secure communication channels and safeguard critical data from unauthorized access. The TDS utilizes Google BigQuery to analyze extensive IoT data for trained threat detection and mitigation decisions. Some necessary algorithms, such as Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and autoencoders-reinforce its functionality. DQN separates devices exhibiting atypical behavior, and autoencoders identify anomalies in device activity, network traffic, and access patterns. The technology quarantines the damaged device to avoid further damage, using safe data processing in Azure Cloud under strict encryption procedures. The TDS continually analyses data streams in real-time, instantly notifying administrators through a mobile application when abnormalities arise and autonomously upgrading security policies to address evolving threats. This research shows the essential function of cloud-based security solutions and artificial intelligence in safeguarding smart home ecosystems against evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Novel AI-Genetics Algorithm for Renewable Bioenergy Generation in City Centers
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Transforming cities into net producers of energy allows urban environments to mitigate the challenges of climate change. Such a transformation requires navigating efficient typologies of new ecosystems and buildings by integrating renewable energy sources into existing infrastructure. Bioenergy is among such sources that harness solar energy to produce biomass, act as natural carbon sinks, and generate oxygen through photosynthesis to improve air quality and support urban resilience. This study constructed a full-scale bioenergy system, with real-time biomass monitoring facilitated by an RGB image-based technique. Neural Networks were then integrated into Genetic Algorithms to improve search efficiency and reduce optimization time. Datasets containing fewer than 100 points exhibited lower predictive accuracy, with a 10-point Neural Network yielding a correlation coefficient of 0.661, and a 50-point Neural Network showing a correlation coefficient of 0.599. As the dataset size increased beyond 150 points, the Neural Network achieved a perfect linear correlation, reflected in a correlation coefficient of 1. Neural Network-Aided Genetic Algorithm optimized the system in just 6 minutes, a remarkable enhancement over the original algorithm that required 24.4 hours. Overall, the study highlights the potential of integrating AI-driven optimization and monitoring techniques into bioenergy systems, contributing to sustainable building designs that enhance renewable bioenergy production.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Cancer Analysis: A Secure and Innovative Approach to Early Diagnosis and Prognosis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of SANAD, a web-based solution aimed at revolutionizing early cancer diagnosis and patient care through artificial intelligence. The system integrates AI-powered diagnostic tool, a patient support chatbot, and advanced cybersecurity measures to offer a comprehensive approach to cancer detection. By leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and large language model, SANAD can analyze medical images and assist healthcare professionals with high diagnostic accuracy. The platform also supports cancer patients through real-time, AI-assisted responses to their medical queries. The paper discusses the challenges in cancer detection, presents the architecture of the SANAD system, and outlines the security protocols to protect sensitive medical data.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Human Factors Approach to Pedestrian Accidents Analysis in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the causes of pedestrian accidents in Amman city from 2014 to 2023 using Human Factors models, including the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), Systems-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP), and the Haddon Matrix Model, Additionally, a Random Forest computational model was applied to predict pedestrian injury severity, offering data-driven insights into accident outcomes. The study identifies the key human, environmental, and organizational factors contributing to pedestrian fatalities and injuries by analyzing accident data and categorizing it within these frameworks. Findings suggest that there should be a focus on unsafe acts by drivers, and road design conditions play a critical role in pedestrian accidents. Recommendations focus on infrastructure improvements, training and Traffic cultural programs, and stakeholder engagement to mitigate these issues. The integration of such computational approaches can enhance predictive accuracy and support smarter urban safety planning.

articleTitle: Zero-Trust Architecture for Smart City Healthcare Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
