abstract: This paper introduces a tailored Zero-Trust Architecture (ZTA) for healthcare systems in smart cities, addressing the security challenges posed by interconnected infrastructures. The model enforces continuous access validation through micro-segmentation, identity and access management (IAM) with multi-factor authentication (MFA), and device trust verification, significantly reducing vulnerabilities. AI-powered real-time monitoring and anomaly detection enhance the system's ability to identify and mitigate advanced persistent threats (APTs) and insider risks. Secure communication protocols, end-to-end encryption, and audit logging ensure data protection, regulatory compliance, and forensic capabilities. The proposed ZTA provides a scalable, future-proof solution that strengthens patient data security and safeguards healthcare infrastructure against evolving cyber threats in smart cities.

articleTitle: Interactive AI for Advancing and Generating Women's Traditional Fashion in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This research sought to safeguard the cultural legacy of women's traditional attire in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by developing a comprehensive digital platform for the collection and categorization of these costumes. The emphasis was placed on the Western region of Saudi Arabia, where a dataset of traditional garments was collected, compiled, and generated. Moreover, a specialized website was created to streamline the marketing and purchasing processes for these traditional outfits. The methodology integrated both descriptive-analytical and experimental approaches based on generative AI. Tools utilized in this research included an expert opinion survey aimed at understanding the requirements for implementing an artificial intelligence-based classification system for women's traditional clothing, as well as measuring user perceptions regarding the website's effectiveness in marketing Saudi Arabia's traditional wear. Additionally, questionnaires were distributed to gather input from specialists concerning the classification system and its related website, focusing on advancing production and marketing strategies. Users' feedback on both the AI-driven classification system and the website was also collected. Key findings indicated that it is viable to preserve cultural heritage represented by traditional garments from Saudi Arabia's western region through their collection and organization within an AI-based framework. Furthermore, this study highlighted opportunities for promoting and selling traditional fashion via a website equipped with an AI classification system. The AI-driven classification system demonstrated remarkable accuracy, approaching 97%, with an error rate of around 3.15%. The conclusion includes recommendations for sharing this system with fashion houses interested in producing traditional women's clothing in Saudi Arabia, along with providing access to databases that could assist in designing and manufacturing such apparel.

articleTitle: Performance and Implementation Comparison of Knuth-Morris-Pratt and Boyer-Moore String Search Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: String search algorithms play an important role in many research areas such as data mining and bioinformatics. While there exist a number of algorithms that handles the topic, we are exploring the the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) and Boyer-Moore algorithms due to their efficiency and versatility. In this work, we compared the algorithms in terms of characteristics, performance and implementation details. We also tested both the algorithms with various patterns and texts that differs in size. We also analyzed the performance of the algorithms on 4 different processors to understand the technological advancements effects on their performance. Our findings suggest that the BM algorithm perform better with large texts and patterns, while the KMP algorithm is better suited for smaller ones. Also, while newer processor generally exhibit improved performance, the significance of these enhancements may vary. Thus, we should rather be looking specific architectural advancements within generations rather than focusing solely on the generational gap.

articleTitle: Review on Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Recognizing Arabic Sign Language
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Sign language is important to enable communication for people with hearing impairments. Over the past few years, artificial intelligence technologies have opened the door to designing models, which can help these individuals become more integrated and engaged into societies. these technologies can also increase their contribution as members to society. This paper provides a review of some of the AI methods used for sign language recognition, especially Arabic Sign Language (ArSL). It focuses on traditional machine learning, deep learning (including convolutional neural networks), transfer learning, and vision transformation models. The paper highlights the emergence of hybrid models that combine different artificial intelligence technologies using all architectural strength. This review emphasizes the growing potential of artificial intelligence technologies to revolutionize Arabic Sign Language recognition and suggests trends for future studies to improve the integration of the hearing impaired into society. This paper can be beneficial to the research of ASL.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Transformer and transfer learning transfer learning

articleTitle: An AI Analytical Model for Human's Posture Analysis: Posture Correction with MediaPipe
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The posture analysis has received considerable interest across various fields such as healthcare, sports science, and human-computer interaction due to its impact on physical performance, prevention of injuries, and ergonomic design. This paper seeks to deliver a thorough overview of the datasets available specifically for posture analysis, emphasizing their appropriateness for training and assessing machine learning models in pose estimation tasks. We systematically classify the existing datasets, including those related to diverse scenarios like sports, everyday activities, and medical evaluations, taking into account aspects such as dataset size, diversity, annotation quality, and the inclusion of temporal data. Additionally, we evaluate the applicability of each dataset in responding to specific research inquiries while outlining their advantages and drawbacks. We also address common evaluation metrics used in posture analysis-such as accuracy, mean average precision (mAP), and percentage of correct keypoints (PCK)-and discuss their utility in validating model performance across varying datasets. Through this synthesis of information, we aim to assist researchers and practitioners in selecting suitable datasets for their studies on posture analysis, thereby aiding the progression of this field within both academic and industrial contexts. This system identifies an individual from an optimal side perspective and assesses the tilt of the neck and torso concerning a designated reference axis. It tracks the angle of inclination as the individual bends beyond a specified threshold. Additional functionalities include tracking the duration of specific postures and ensuring proper camera alignment. The package includes a solution script designed to implement an alert system for poor posture, utilizing MediaPipe Pose Solution and OpenCV.

articleTitle: YOLO Meets FedAVG: A Privacy-Preserving Approach to Autonomous Vehicles Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) systems rely heavily on accurate object detection to ensure safe and efficient operation, with models like YOLO excelling in real-time performance and precision. However, in the context of AV applications, traditional centralized object detection methods often struggle with data privacy concerns and the need for generalization across diverse, dynamic environments. Existing research predominantly focuses on centralized approaches, which lack sufficient privacy measures and face limitations in scalability when applied to decentralized, real-world settings. To address these challenges, we propose a privacy-preserving framework that integrates YOLOv8 with the Federated Averaging (FedAVG) algorithm, allowing decentralized training across multiple AV units while retaining data privacy. This approach trains the model locally over 10 epochs per client, followed by aggregation over 10 communication rounds, enhancing detection accuracy while meeting privacy requirements critical to AV deployment. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our YOLOv8-FedAVG framework, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 86%, precision of 84%, and recall of 83%, showcasing its potential to advance AV object detection in a scalable, privacy-focused manner.

articleTitle: Assessment of Mechanical and Antimicrobial Properties of Die-Cast Al Scrap-Cu Alloy for Contact Surface Application
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Contact surface bacterial infections are on the increase globally. Metallic silver and copper with excellent antibacterial properties have been reported in the literature but seldom use for structural application due to high cost and relative scarcity. In this work, Al-xwt%Cu alloys with 2.5, 7.5, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, and 25.0 wt% Cu were developed and produced via die-casting technique with mould pre-heating temperature of 300°C. Mechanical and antimicrobial properties of the die-cast Al-xCu products were investigated following standard procedure. The results revealed an enhancement in tensile and compressive strength of the alloy with increase in wt% addition of Cu up to 20 wt% and thereafter decline. The peak yield tensile and compressive strength of 200.641 and 373.26 MPa which falls within the recommended value of 110–240 MPa for structural handrail contact surface application was recorded in the sample with 20% wt Cu addition in aluminum thus obtaining a 538 and 80% improvement respectively compared to control sample with 0% Cu. Results of antimicrobial property of the developed Al-xCu alloy antimicrobial property enhancement and the performance is dependent on the specific exposed bacteria strains and weight concentration of Cu. The efficacy of antibacterial assessment of Al-xCu alloy indicated the addition of Cu beyond 20 wt% relative to control sample within each bacteria yielded 238, 141, 95 and 94% antibacterial enhancement on Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli respectively. Hence Escherichia coli has more resistance to the antibacterial property of Al-xCu alloy

articleTitle: A Systemic Review of Healthcare Challenges Due to Ethical Implications: A PRISMA Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In this rapidly evolving field of healthcare, Artificial Intelligence(AI) presents significant ethical challenges. There is an urgent need to address these ethical concerns as they are directly affecting patient care, As per Healthcare Tech Outlook, 80% of healthcare data cannot be used as it is not structured, resulting in biased outcomes due to its inability to be analyzed. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare has the potential to revolutionize medical services, enhancing patient outcomes, operational efficiency, and overall healthcare management. However, this technological advancement also introduces significant ethical challenges that must be addressed to ensure responsible and equitable use. This research explores the systemic impacts of AI ethics in healthcare by examining five key themes: ethical challenges, influential contributors and collaboration networks, emerging themes, cooccurrence of ethical concepts, and influential publications. The study identifies critical ethical issues such as bias, privacy, transparency, and accountability, highlighting the need for robust ethical guidelines. It also maps the contributions of leading authors and institutions, revealing collaboration networks that drive research in this field. Emerging themes such as transparency, data privacy, fairness, and the environmental impact of AI are discussed, reflecting the evolving landscape of AI ethics. The cooccurrence of ethical concepts is analyzed to understand their interconnected nature, emphasizing the complexity of ethical AI implementation. Finally, influential publications are reviewed to assess their impact on the development of ethical guidelines and best practices. By addressing these research themes, the study aims to contribute to the development of comprehensive ethical frameworks for AI in healthcare, ensuring that the benefits of this technology are realized while minimizing potential risks and ethical concerns.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Communication Protocols in Blockchain-IoT Systems for Optimizing IoT Data Flow Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is considered an evolving technology, consisting of different types of connected devices that have sensors, specialized hardware, and software. However, considerable challenges related to user data privacy, security, and device integrity are presented by this swift expansion, with digital identity being identified as a significant concern in the online landscape. Established by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) [2], Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) represent a standardized format for defining identity. A peer-to-peer model for managing identity and credentials through self-sovereign identity is facilitated by DIDs, in conjunction with blockchain technology and public-key cryptography. The development of verifiable credentials is enabled by the combination of DIDs and blockchain technology, allowing for the verification of the identities of transacting parties through distributed identity registration and the identification of cryptographic keys necessary for validating electronic authentication during transactions. This integrated framework is regarded as both reliable and trusted. Device registration, verification, and credential revocation are enabled by it. In addition, security is ensured, the privacy of participating nodes is respected, and data integrity is upheld to address several existing challenges, such as data scalability and confidentiality. Trusted management and transaction of IoT data are ensured by the presented IoT data platform. Blockchain, decentralized identifiers, and public key cryptography are integrated by the authors to develop this platform. Self-sovereign identity is granted to each participating device, and dynamic changes in components like consensus algorithms and databases are supported by key features. Different IoT communication protocols are evaluated within a decentralized blockchain infrastructure for identity verification by the authors, focusing on interactions between IoT devices and networked servers through wireless connections. The Hyper ledger framework is used to implement blockchain. Consequently, subsequent optimization solutions are proposed to expand the platform's application range and improve the efficiency of IoT data management.

articleTitle: Privacy in Smart Digital Healthcare During Hajj and Umrah: Challenges and Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Makkah is one of the five smart cities in Saudi Arabia, annually welcoming millions of Muslims for Hajj and Umrah. Among the primary services offered to those performing Hajj and Umrah is smart digital healthcare. It can ensure faster identification of people needing medical help within large crowds usually formed during peak Umrah times and Hajj. However, several privacy challenges exist within the realm of smart digital healthcare. For instance, an ongoing privacy challenge is collecting and processing health data. Past incidents showed that unauthorized access to patients' health data could reveal users' private information, including personally identifiable information. In this paper, we explore these challenges that may hinder the sustainable delivery of smart digital healthcare services during Hajj and Umrah. Then, we analyze Sehhaty, the official healthcare platform in Saudi Arabia, with regard to the presented challenges by examining Sehhaty's privacy policy, privacy settings, and users' reviews. We observe that Sehhaty attempts to provide answers to these challenges by explaining the privacy practices in its privacy policies. However, Sehhaty does not adequately address the privacy preferences challenge as it only offers one privacy option to all users. We provide recommendations on how the mentioned privacy challenges can be properly addressed.

articleTitle: Selfish-Free Influential Nodes Detection in Mobile Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Mobile networks where users group in communities based on their interests, and disseminate data mainly to their community using their mobile devices, are called Mobile Social Networks (MSN). However, the efficiency of data dissemination becomes a challenging problem in these networks. Using influential users can improve the efficiency of data dissemination. An influential user should have an effective activity on the network and influence other users. The participation behavior of nodes in the network dramatically affects the detection process of influential nodes. Self-sufficient nodes who selectively participate in the dissemination of data in the network may reduce the influence of the other nodes. This paper proposes detecting influential nodes that consider the negative effects of selfish behavior. The performance analysis of the proposed selfish-free influential node detection protocol is presented by comparing it to another one that does not consider the selfishness problem. This comparison shows that the proposed protocol achieves efficiency up to 30% in a environment of selfish behavior.

articleTitle: Precision Farming with Autonomous Drones: Real-time Data and Efficient Fertilization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The study explores the challenges farmers face due to environmental issues and the growing global population. It suggests that digital technologies, particularly drones, can improve agricultural productivity. The research focuses on developing a drone capable of autonomously fertilizing fields, providing real-time data and insights. With Raspberry Pi, multispectral sensors, GPS technology, CNN, Tiny Yolo v4, and AI-driven analytics, the drone can deliver chemicals to targeted areas and return to its base station, significantly reducing farmers' efforts. This model conducted four tests to evaluate the drone's accuracy in a 60 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> cropland area. It utilized a single drone, although cooperative operation with multiple drones could enhance efficiency. As a result, the findings show that optimal results were achieved with a load of 500 grams at a speed of 28 km/h, achieving an overall precision fertilization accuracy rate of 98.3%. This payload is sufficient for small-scale operations, but its efficiency depends on crop density and the required fertilization level. The drone can operate continuously for 20 minutes at full capacity. In the test period, with a fly time of 3.86 minutes, the drone covered approximately 59 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> cropland area. Compared to traditional human labor, the drone demonstrates higher precision and reduces environmental impact by minimizing chemical waste. The experiment was conducted in a controlled agricultural field to simulate realistic farming conditions. The use of drones in field inspection and pesticide application is examined in this study, emphasizing the methodology, controllers, and hardware/software components. It illustrates how AI and machine learning improve agriculture's technical efficiency and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Energy Recovery and Power Management in EVs Using Supercapacitors and Regenerative Braking
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Regenerative braking (RB) is crucial in enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of electric vehicles (EVs) by converting kinetic energy into usable electric energy during braking. However, current systems face challenges in maximizing energy recovery and managing power effectively. This research presents an optimized regenerative braking system that combines the benefits of supercapacitors and Brushless DC (BLDC) motors to improve energy recovery efficiency. The study introduces advanced control algorithms for BLDC motors to ensure precise and reliable operation across various driving conditions. Furthermore, refined power management strategies are developed to optimize energy storage between supercapacitors and batteries, enhancing overall system efficiency. The proposed model employs modern control techniques and power management solutions, allowing for real-time energy optimization during braking. With an overall energy recovery efficiency of 92.5%, the system shows significant promise in minimizing energy losses and supporting the sustainability goals of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Intrusion Detection: Recent Advances and Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: With the development of technologies and increasing security threats, intrusion detection systems have become more critical in detecting and protecting operations from attacks. Deep learning has significantly contributed to advancements in intrusion detection, especially through reinforcement learning systems. This survey reviews the concepts of intrusion detection and Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems in intrusion detection (ID), with a focus on recent advancements using techniques such as Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Adversarial Reinforcement Learning (AE-RL), and Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL). We also emphasize the crucial role of feature engineering in conjunction with RL techniques. By examining these cutting-edge approaches and their integration with advanced feature engineering methods, we aim to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of the art in reinforcement learning-based intrusion detection systems and their potential to enhance cybersecurity measures. In addition to exploring the applications of reinforcement learning and feature engineering in intrusion detection, we highlight and analyze the most well-known databases used in this field, offering insights into the data resources that drive the development and evaluation of these advanced security systems.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Driven Smart Cities: Review of Key Applications and Emerging Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The future of blockchain technology holds significant promise across various sectors, driven by its inherent decentralisation, transparency, and security capabilities. As industries increasingly recognise the potential benefits, the global blockchain market is projected to grow substantially. Concurrently, the smart city concept has gained significant traction worldwide, as governments and corporations aspire to create urban environments that leverage technology to enhance efficiency and quality of life. In this regard, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution, offering decentralised, secure, and transparent data management which is critical for the sustainable development of smart cities. This review paper explores the integration of blockchain technology in smart city frameworks which is considered timely. It further synthesises findings from recent literature in blockchain applications across six key components of smart cities: digital infrastructure, urban mobility, public safety, public health, environmental resource management, and governance. As cities evolve to meet the demands of rapid urbanisation, the decentralised and immutable nature of blockchain offers unique advantages for building transparent, secure, and efficient urban ecosystems. This paper also examines possible future trends that point towards a future where blockchain serves as a foundational layer in smart city infrastructure. By summarising current applications and identifying future research directions, this review paper provides a comprehensive resource for future researchers and policymakers who are aiming to leverage blockchain in the development of resilient and citizen-focused urban environments.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Security Against Deepfakes by Using Multimodal Detection: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Technology has become an essential component of daily life, with millions of people placing their trust in it. Security is important, especially in maximizing the optimization of face recognition (FR) technology, since it has been an enormous concern. The process of recognizing people from images or video clips occurs by using algorithms that detect and extract distinctive facial features. This paper provides a comprehensive study of FR security threats, by reviewing multiple algorithms and Deep Learning (DL) approaches in the facial recognition field. The point of this paper is to discuss the challenge posed by facial spoofing attacks, using either 2D or 3D masks. In this paper we demonstrated different implementations of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) algorithms to address the complexity of deep fake detection, focusing on their varied methodologies for facial detection and recognition. The paper emphasizes on the importance of the CNNs and ANNs algorithms using the Inception V3 and ResNet-50 models that helps learn, verify, and recognize face images to enhance the results to be more accurate through using the precise models in common areas such as gates surveillance. Furthermore, different models will be discussed in the paper along with Inception V3 which obtained the maximum testing results based on high performance when interacting in various image environments and high reliability in handling complex data.

articleTitle: Autonomous Firefighting Robot: Design and Implementation for Hazardous Environment Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of a robotic system designed to assist firefighters in assessing hazardous environments, aiming to improve safety and operational efficiency. The prototype, modeled as a car, autonomously evaluates fire-affected areas using Arduino microcontroller technology, integrating temperature and smoke sensors to monitor critical parameters like heat levels and smoke density in real-time. An ultrasonic sensor ensures precise navigation by detecting obstacles and dynamically adjusting movement to prevent collisions. Powered by high-capacity batteries, DC motors, and a DC driver, the robot demonstrates reliable mobility in all directions. A Bluetooth module facilitates seamless wireless communication with a control program developed in Visual Studio using C#, enabling remote operation and environmental monitoring. The robot also features a buzzer for auditory alerts and multi-color LED indicators to provide clear visual signals about environmental conditions to users and bystanders. The prototype successfully implements these functionalities, showcasing its potential as a preliminary model.

articleTitle: AI-Based Zero Trust Architecture for Cognitive City Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The rapid development of cognitive cities, which leverage artificial intelligence (AI) and interconnected smart systems, introduces significant security challenges due to their complex and dynamic infrastructure. Traditional security models that rely on fixed perimeters and implicit trust are insufficient to protect the diverse range of services, from smart transportation to IoT-powered utilities, in cognitive city environments. In this paper, we propose an AI-Based Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) designed to secure the multilayered, interconnected networks of cognitive cities. Our framework assumes that no entity, human or machine, can be trusted by default and integrates AI-driven mechanisms for continuous authentication, realtime access control, and proactive threat detection. The proposed AI-powered ZTA utilizes dynamic authentication protocols based on multi-factor and behavioral biometrics to constantly verify identities. It incorporates AI models for context-aware access control, continuously adapting security policies in real time based on user behavior, environmental conditions, and risk factors. Additionally, AI enhances micro-segmentation, enabling the city's network to be divided into smaller, isolated segments to contain potential threats. Through real-time monitoring and AI-driven anomaly detection, our architecture continuously scans for abnormal activities across IoT networks, smart infrastructure, and critical services, proactively mitigating threats before they escalate. AI's predictive capabilities also play a key role in anticipating insider threats and ensuring device trustworthiness by analyzing communication patterns and security vulnerabilities in endpoints. This paper presents a detailed system design, outlining how AI models can be integrated into Zero Trust principles to provide scalable and adaptive security for cognitive cities. We demonstrate the application of our framework through several use cases, including autonomous vehicle networks, smart energy grids, and IoT-based healthcare systems. Moreover, we address challenges such as scalability, real-time decisionmaking, and privacy concerns. Our findings suggest that an AI-enhanced Zero Trust Architecture not only strengthens the cybersecurity posture of cognitive cities but also offers a unified, automated, and selfadaptive framework capable of responding to evolving threats in real time. This research contributes to the advancement of smart city security by presenting an innovative approach that merges AI with Zero Trust principles, offering a robust solution for safeguarding future urban infrastructures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Logistics Through IoT-Integrated NFC-Based Smart Post Boxes for Resilient Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This paper examines the shift in consumer preferences regarding NFC-based Smart Post Boxes as a concept evaluated in both pre- and post-COVID-19 contexts. The study focuses on the Czech Republic, assessing the economic viability and environmental impacts of these systems. Key findings indicate a 91.72% increase in operational savings and a 10.87% reduction in the payback period, from 1.27 years to 1.13 years. Additionally, there is a 114.04% reduction in externalities, including emissions, noise pollution, and traffic congestion, demonstrating the system's potential to support urban sustainability and efficiency. These results highlight the evolving consumer interest in contactless delivery solutions and the feasibility of further developing NFC-based Smart Post Boxes within smart city frameworks.

articleTitle: Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for URL Phishing Detection: Protect Users
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The growing threat of URL phishing attacks raises the need for advanced detection systems to safeguard digital environments. This paper explores the effectiveness of various machine learning models for classifying URLs as phishing or be-nign, focusing on the Random Forest model. Leveraging ensemble learning, Random Forest demonstrated superior accuracy and reliability compared to traditional methods, achieving consistent performance with accuracy rates between 99.93% and 99.97%. The model's performance was evaluated daily over eight days and compared against other machine learning models, highlighting its robustness in handling real-world scenarios. The study utilized GridSearchCV to optimize model hyperparameters, enhancing their robustness and minimizing overfitting. Future research directions include advanced feature engineering, deep learning techniques, and multi-modal data integration to improve phishing detection systems further.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Panel Efficiency through Advanced Dust Detection: A Comparative Study of VGG16, VGG19, and Inception V3 Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Solar panel efficiency must be given serious consideration when working to create sustainable energy solutions. This paper tackles another threat to proper energy generation due to the accumulation of dust on solar panels. This study tackles a novel image-processing method with three state-of-art convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures including VGG16, VGG19, and Inception V3. The models were evaluated on their effectiveness in detecting and classifying dust coverage on solar panels, using a dataset of more than 700 images taken from solar power facilities. The accuracy of detection of model VGG16 was 96.5%, and VGG19 provided the accuracy of 97.2% which enhanced the accuracy from the VGG16. Inception V3, which is well known for the efficiency with which it deals with complex image data, outperformed both with an accuracy of 98.3%. We conclude that the application of these advanced CNN architectures can help improve sustainability and efficiency by providing accurate, timely detections of dust accumulation on solar panels with our model. Not only did this research enhance our knowledge on solar panel maintenance, but it also adds another use case of CNNs in applications for sustainable energy systems. This approach not only lowers operational costs but also greatly enhances the system's productivity and reliability.

articleTitle: NutriMo: An Android Application for Monitoring Child Growth and Preventing Stunting Using Forward Chaining Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Stunting is a chronic condition that affects the growth and development of children under 5 years old, leading to various health and cognitive issues. In Indonesia, the prevalence of stunting remains high, with a target to reduce it to 14% by 2024. This study aims to design an Android-based nutrition monitoring system using the forward chaining algorithm to support the prevention and management of stunting. The system utilizes data on a child's age, sex, weight, and height to determine their growth condition and provide personalized nutritional recommendations. The development process involved literature study, expert consultation, data collection, system design using UML, and implementation in Java for Android. The accuracy of the system was assessed by comparing its results with manual assessments by a nutritionist, yielding good performance across 14 trials. The Nutrition Monitoring (NutriMo) application has the potential to assist parents and healthcare providers in tracking children's growth and preventing stunting. Future work can focus on expanding the application's features and conducting larger-scale validation studies.

articleTitle: Innovating NCAAA Accreditation: A Smart Education Management System Powered by Generative Pre-trained Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study introduces a smart education management system designed to enhance the accreditation processes mandated by the National Commission for Academic Accreditation & Assessment (NCAAA) for postgraduate programs. By leveraging Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) models, the system efficiently generates comprehensive course reports and dynamic assessment questions, aligning them with the cognitive levels defined in Bloom's Taxonomy. Automating these critical but labor-intensive tasks significantly improves the efficiency of accreditation processes in academic settings. Initial testing within the Computer Science Department at King Abdulaziz University (KAU) demonstrated the system's robustness and scalability, indicating its potential for broader application across universities. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) not only streamlines administrative processes but also improves the quality of educational assessments through alignment with Bloom's Taxonomy. This study emphasizes the transformative potential of AI in educational accreditation, setting a new benchmark for future research and development in integrating AI technologies for smart education management systems.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Microservices Architecture in Comparison with SOA and Monolithic Models
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: These days, requirements are growing faster than ever, and new technologies are being adopted, making systems bigger, more expensive, and more complex. Finding a suitable architecture for software creation in the last few years has been challenging. In software development, microservices architecture, or MSA, has emerged as the newest trend. Microservice-based applications scale horizontally well and enable the company to keep smaller, more agile development teams. The distributed nature of the microservice architecture has several limitations and disadvantages in addition to its many advantages. This research paper comprehensively examines microservices architecture with service-oriented and monolithic models by previously implemented models, where it is visible that, in most cases, microservices architecture works efficiently. In some instances, monolithic and Service-oriented architecture(SOA) also produces similar efficiency based on the application size. However, people still need to gain the proper knowledge to implement a microservices architecture. As a new technology, MSA has many drawbacks, and security is one of the significant issues that needs to be resolved. This study also discusses some potential advantages of microservices architecture. Among them, scaling is the most desirable property for different industries in developing applications or systems.

articleTitle: A Survey on Protecting Users Against Phishing Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Phishing attacks are a form of cyberattack that involves sending malicious emails, texts, or websites with the goal of obtaining confidential information or gaining access to a user's accounts and systems. These attacks have become increasingly prevalent over the years and represent a significant security threat for both individuals and organizations. This paper presents a survey of different strategies for protecting users from such threats by understanding the underlying mechanisms used in phishing attacks and exploring possible countermeasures that can be implemented. The paper also conducts and analyzes existing algorithms on phishing attack mechanisms and countermeasures, with particular emphasis on emerging trends and approaches being used in modern phishing campaigns. This will provide important insight into how attackers are operating as well as any existing countermeasures that can be further improved upon. The paper shows also different datasets that have been used in these algorithms.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Manufacturing Industry: Assessment, Challenges, and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In this work we evaluate the state of the semiconductor manufacturing industry and its challenges and trends. Future trends in the industry are analyzed from three perspectives: the evolution of Industry 4.0, the advances in semiconductor materials, and the impact of the Covid-19 Pandemic. The semiconductor manufacturing industry witnessed an acute decline in the United States and other regions in the two decades prior to the CoVid-19 pandemic. The decline was only uncovered after the chip shortage of 2021 that resulted from the severe supply chain disruption. Trends in the industry were analyzed from three perspectives: Industry 4.0, advances in materials, and the Post-pandemic era. As a result of the evolution of the fourth generation of industry (Industry 4.0), trends in semiconductor manufacturing include robotization, which caused the industry to become the largest market for industrial robotics since 2020, and an all-time peak globalization. The semiconductor industry is a very globalized industry with corporates from different parts of the world taking part in the production of the final product. Although some materials such as carbon and Gallium Nitride show promising trends to replace silicon as the material of choice. It will likely not be before two or three decades when a semiconductor material will be able to replace silicon. Challenges for the industry include the shortage of the trained-workforce, and the added inter-country restrictions that may hinder the globalization of the industry.

articleTitle: Molecular Precision Diagnostic Medicine in Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Improving healthcare services for cancer detection is a priority. Each country prioritizes the enhancement of healthcare services geared towards cancer detection, as it is essential for both healthcare professionals and patients to comprehend and depend upon. Faced when a patient has clear symptoms or cancerous tumors on the outside of the body, extremely basic and rudimentary methods are used, such as imaging or physical examination, and there is little focus on advanced techniques such as molecular diagnostics for cancer. However, such approaches have major limitations in their specific diagnostic accuracy. Although these approaches may pick up visible tumors or those with abnormal test results, they are very ineffective in dealing with more subtle organic or genetic tumors, especially in the early stages. Because these strategies use abnormal markers and clinical findings, especially diagnostics, any malignant tumor that does not have prominent markers may be detected at an advanced stage when it has progressed and become critical.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Air Traffic Control for Drones in Urban Areas: AI-Driven Route Optimization and Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The growth of drone and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) use in cities brings a new set of challenges to safely manage air traffic in crowded urban skies. This research proposes an innovative IoT-enabled and AI-driven air traffic control system designed specifically to meet the unique demands of urban drone applications such as deliveries, surveillance and disaster response. The proposed system integrates advanced AI techniques, namely Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for decentralized control, Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) for adaptive routing and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for multi-objective optimization. These methodologies enable real-time route optimization, collision avoidance and energy efficiency. A combination of three-dimensional (3D) urban navigation and Voronoi-based geofencing helps in avoiding obstacles and restricted areas. This proposed system also incorporates IoT-based battery monitoring for real-time energy management and utilizes hybrid communication networks to maintain seamless operations in high-density urban airspaces. Cellular, satellite and local access make for effective and dependable delivery of the communication network. Weather conditions are used in optimization to achieve adaptive routing. Case studies illustrate the practical implementation of this scalable framework, highlighting its ability to enhance safety, operational efficiency and sustainability in urban UAV operations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models in Solidity Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection: Review
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Blockchain (BC) technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are promising areas with potential for powerful, secure, and decentralized applications in various sectors. Also, LLMs, are essential advanced machine learning frameworks, which are now used in various applications, including customer service, chatbots, code generation, and language translation. In terms of software development, LLMs are being investigated as a potential way to create smart contracts, focusing on their ability to emulate human programming techniques. For that purpose, this study reviews the capabilities and limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-3.5, PaLM2, and Code Llama in detecting vulnerabilities in Solidity smart contract code.

articleTitle: A High-Performance 5G/6G Framework for Smart Cities Supporting Multi-Level Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The evolution of Smart Cities hinges on robust 5G/6G networks that provide the foundational infrastructure for real-time, data-driven services and automation across urban landscapes. This paper explores the essential role of advanced communication systems in facilitating smart city applications such as emergency response, mobility services, environmental monitoring, and autonomous vehicles. Leveraging multi-access edge computing (MEC) and multi-level artificial intelligence (AI), the proposed 5G/6G platform supports mission-critical applications requiring low latency, high bandwidth, and reliable connectivity. Through network slicing, dedicated virtual networks are tailored to specific urban services, enabling efficient data management and optimized resource allocation. Additionally, this framework promotes layered AI processing across MEC and cloud nodes, allowing localized decision-making while aggregating data for long-term city planning. The paper further details key use cases and technical architecture diagrams, illustrating the integration of AI, MEC, and network slicing as transformative elements in building resilient, adaptive urban ecosystems. This approach not only enhances public safety, transportation, and resource management but also provides scalable, future-proof solutions for the next generation of urban infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Framework for Overcoming Data Accessibility Challenges in Urban Microgrids for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Smart grid-connected urban microgrids can prove crucial for integrating distributed renewable energy resources, reducing dependency on the utility grid, increasing the democratization of energy in the smart city, and enabling local energy exchanges, among other things. However, their success often hinges on accessing historical and real-time data from active prosumers. The challenge is aggravated when collecting this data from residential end-users. We have identified common hurdles in microgrid establishment and followed a standard approach to evaluate techno-economic aspects using data from existing wind turbines. To address these obstacles and foster microgrid growth, we propose an innovative, interoperable framework leveraging cutting-edge IT solutions. Proposed framework is capable of mitigating the documented challenges and facilitating easy access to desired energy data, thereby enhancing the viability and attractiveness of microgrids for private investors.

articleTitle: Protecting Privacy and Securing Smart Home Network based on Zero Trust Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The main goal of utilizing IoT technology in smart homes is to enhance convenience and flexibility. However, despite the numerous benefits, there are certain vulnerabilities and flaws that can jeopardize security and privacy. This research explores how Zero Trust Network (ZTN) technology can be implemented in smart homes to address crucial objectives such as privacy and security. The study focuses on developing and continuously verifying a ZTN-based system. A key challenge addressed in the research is optimizing security by categorizing home resources and devices based on their importance. To improve the efficiency of verification, authorization, and authentication processes, the research proposes algorithms that utilize Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC) and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). The simulation results demonstrate that in a Device-to- Device scenario, the attack detection success rates using ABAC and ECC are 87.28% and 94.30%, respectively. These findings suggest that implementing a Zero Trust Network in smart homes can significantly enhance security and privacy for homeowners, protecting them from potential attacks.

articleTitle: Quick Park: Integrated Sensor-Based Smart Parking System with Chatbot for Enhanced Urban Mobility and Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The traffic problems are accelerating due to an increase in the number of vehicles on the road. Consequently, the availability of vacant parking slots has long been a frustrating and time-consuming challenge for drivers, especially in metropolitan areas. Searching for vacant parking space is a prevalent issue thus affecting the mental health of the drivers and also leading to the wastage of the fuel consumed while searching for the available parking slot. This situation creates the need for some smart that can address the parking problem faced by the drivers. Hence, this study proposes an IoT-based smart solution named Quick Park which is a smart parking finder application. The system incorporates strategically placed sensors in parking areas, which communicate with a mobile application to provide real-time information on parking availability. By leveraging sensor technology, drivers can easily and quickly locate vacant parking spots, eliminating the need for aimless driving and uncertainty. The proposed IoT-based smart parking system will offer a reliable and efficient solution to address the limitations of existing systems. The sensor-enabled smart parking finder presents a convenient and effective solution to the problem of finding parking spaces, ultimately improving the efficiency and ease of urban mobility. The deployment of the proposed solution will lead to the efficient utilization of resources and it will also contribute towards the improvement of the mental health of drivers by relieving the stress of the scarcity of parking space.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Environment with Reinforcement Learning-Based on Traffic Control
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Transportation networks in smart cities are considered as one criteria of quality of life. This paper discusses Digital Twins (DTs) adopted in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) domain, especially traffic management systems in smart cities. DTs is done by collecting and analyzing massive amounts of data from various sources such as cameras, sensors, and Global Position System (GPS), where Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and predictive analytics are performed on these systems. In this paper, we discussed different types of methodologies such as inverted pyramid and snowballing methodologies along with security threats of the data that gathered that faced in this area. This study concluded the comparisons of previous algorithms to get the best results in traffic control management systems based on areal practice to develop a traffic intersection located in Alhasa city, Saudi Arabic. As this inverted pyramid algorithm is more reliable as classified the most important data first, and suitable for network data analysis, than the snowballing algorithm.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Applications in Predictive Fetal Health Assessment and Early Intervention
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Fetal health involves monitoring the well-being of the unborn baby, identifying potential complications such as distress, congenital issues and ensuring timely interventions for a healthy pregnancy and successful delivery. This study presents a machine learning framework aimed at improving fetal health predictions with a focus on the need for early detection of complications like fetal distress. Traditional monitoring tools such as cardiotocography and ultrasound, often rely on subjective interpretation, leading to delays or inaccuracies in diagnoses. To tackle these issues, advanced machine learning techniques such as XGBoost, Blending, and Stacking are applied. These models are assessed for their ability to handle complex fetal health data and improve classification accuracy. While Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors show moderate success, XGBoost, Blending, and Stacking perform better, achieving 96% accuracy, reducing errors and enhancing clinical decision-making. For small datasets and generalization issues and using multiple fetal health indicators for stronger predictions. Automated machine learning models offer significant improvements in the speed and precision of fetal health assessments, helping reduce risks for both mother, child and advancing AI applications in prenatal care for improved outcomes.

articleTitle: Social Media Multi-Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Natural language in social media is often ambiguous, carrying diverse perspectives that are critical for opinion analysis. With vast amounts of unstructured data, particularly on platforms like Twitter, it is impractical to manually analyse relevant insights. This rapid data growth has highlighted the need for intelligent filtering and mining techniques in decision support systems to help organizations build brand reputation, foster online communities, and enhance profitability. Multi-Emotion detection is key for capturing implicit user opinions and specific emotional states; however, challenges such as text bipolarity, limited representative feature vectors, and inadequate annotated lexicons often hinder accuracy. This research aims to improve multi-emotion detection accuracy by extracting emotion implied tokens and converting them into feature vectors that capture semantic relevance. Using annotated lexicons, word embeddings, unigrams, and term frequency, these vectors are trained across five machine learning models, which are Naïve Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K- nearest neighbor (KNN), and Multi- layer Percepton (MLP). Finally, two ensemble techniques are applied to refine model outputs, achieving an improvement accuracy over previous work worked. The proposed system, evaluated on a real dataset, achieves a hamming score of 0.55 and an average F1 score of 0.68, demonstrating its potential for effective multi-label emotion detection.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Generation Trends - Insights from Python Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Energy systems around the world have relied heavily on fossil fuels, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental challenges. However, in alignment with global climate objectives, many regions are accelerating their transition toward renewable energy sources. This study examines the evolving energy production landscape in the Netherlands, where fossil fuel-based technologies are steadily being replaced with intermittent renewable sources, particularly solar and wind. This research uses Python for data preprocessing, trend analysis, and visualization to explore key temporal patterns in energy generation. The results reveal that by 2023, nearly half of the Netherlands' electricity demand will be met by renewable sources, with solar and wind energy contributing approximately 17.6% and 15%, respectively. These gains are driven mainly by photovoltaic (PV) projects and offshore wind installations. Despite these positive trends, challenges such as grid stability and negative pricing during periods of excess supply present significant obstacles. Addressing these issues will require innovative solutions to increase the reliability and efficiency of renewable energy supplies. This paper discusses potential strategies, including advanced energy storage and adaptive grid management systems, which can enhance renewable integration and support a resilient infrastructure.

articleTitle: Remote Blood Sampling Collection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: With the use of a cutting-edge technique called remote blood sampling collection, people can donate blood from places other than standard hospital settings, such as their homes. This approach aims to improve patient comfort and compliance, lower healthcare expenses, and boost accessibility. Finger-prick devices, dried blood spot (DBS) sampling, and micro sampling methods that need little blood volume are some of the technologies that make remote blood collection possible. Technological developments in telemedicine and diagnostic technologies facilitate remote collection by enabling medical professionals to monitor and interpret blood sample findings without forcing patients to attend clinical facilities. Patients with chronic diseases, those living in distant places, and others with mobility challenges will find this method especially helpful. Even with its potential, remote blood collection has drawbacks, including maintaining sample integrity, precision in diagnostic testing, and overcoming logistical and legal obstacles. Remote blood sampling has the potential to revolutionize healthcare delivery by increasing efficiency and patient-centeredness. One of the main aims is to activate remote blood sampling collection and connect it to Saudi health systems, such as Sehaty, in line with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's 2030 health goals. By including a remote blood sampling device option in the Sehaty system, patients will be able to request and get the device at home. They will then collect a sample, transmit it to the laboratory, and receive the results via the Sehaty platform.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Autonomy of Soft Robots in Minimally Invasive Surgeries Through Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Researchers have recognized the potential of employing soft robots in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS), which could significantly reduce the side effects associated with traditional surgical methods and enhance patient outcomes. However, the extent to which this potential is realized depends on the level of autonomy achieved by the soft robots. Lower levels of autonomy necessitate increased hands-on involvement during MIS, potentially compromising the robots' ability to perform procedures with consistent accuracy. Consequently, achieving high levels of accuracy in the autonomy of soft robots remains a significant challenge. The autonomy of these robots is influenced by various factors, including their capacity to accurately classify their surroundings, particularly anatomical structures, which is crucial for effective decision-making. To address the challenge posed by our research question, How can the application of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) improve the autonomy of soft robots in performing complex tasks in MIS, particularly in the precise classification of anatomical structures and decision making?, we conducted an in-depth literature review and investigation into the integration of DNNs and DRL within this context. Our study used a modeling and simulation methodology to evaluate and quantify the benefits of incorporating these advanced AI techniques. Through this approach, we measured the effects of DNNs and DRL on enhancing the autonomy of soft robots, particularly in their ability to perform complex tasks in MIS with improved precision and decision-making capabilities. This work represents a step toward optimizing robotic autonomy in surgical environments, potentially leading to more efficient and accurate outcomes in minimally invasive procedures.

articleTitle: CityShield: An IoT-Driven and AI-Based Threat Detection System for Smart City Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In this era of technology, smart cities are becoming more common, but their growing connectivity exposes them to continuous cybersecurity threats, putting their operations and security at risk. This research focuses on enhancing cybersecurity in smart cities by implementing a real-time threat detection and response system, with key metrics such as faster detection speeds, reduced false alarms, and improved system adaptability to evolving threats. Robust safety protocols are required because attacks by ransomware, breaches of information, and weak IoT devices endanger vital services. This research proposes a system that presents the implementation of real-time data collection through IoT devices and a streamlined data flow leveraging Kafka for rapid ingestion, HDFS for scalable long-term storage, and Apache Spark for efficient processing. The proposed system uses Autoencoder algorithms to detect anomalies and DQN to make fast, intelligent decisions responding to detected threats. The proposed system aims to strengthen clever city defenses by continuously monitoring various city services. Robust and adaptable threat detection and response systems that can re-duce vulnerabilities are guaranteed through this technological integration. This versatile system protects vital infrastructure by changing it to counter new cyber threats. It enhances city safety and strengthens smart city cybersecurity by detecting threats and safeguarding critical information and infrastructure for a secure future. With this proposed strategy, smart cities could become safer, more technologically advanced, and more resilient. This proposed solution allows smart cities to become technologically advanced, secure, and resilient.

articleTitle: Data Generation in Healthcare Using Constraint Satisfaction Parameters (CSP)
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: In this research, we examine the synthetic creation, alteration, and enhancement of data through Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI). This inaugural study focused on generating healthy data via GAI for analysis and detection of chronic diseases (Depression, Stress, and Anxiety). Following the generation process using this deep learning approach, we analyze and visualize synthetic data through various metrics. The outcomes of this methodology are expected to yield novel insights into data generation concerning pressure-related diseases (depression, stress, and anxiety). Integrating high-quality synthetic data is anticipated to improve the production of financial transaction data. Finally, the proposed model is evaluated, and the results of the initial GAI model are generated. In this paper, we introduce a specialized generative Transformer language model that has been pre-trained on an extensive collection of medical constraint satisfaction parameters. We assess generation across medical natural language processing tasks and show that it surpasses existing models in most evaluations. Additionally, we offer a comprehensive analysis of the model's limitations by detailing numerous errors and challenges it faces. The mean scores for the produced descriptive data and shape pair trends in continuous columns were around 0.99 and 0.92, respectively. Conversely, the average scores for the categorical text generated in the initial region were notably high. This highlights the GAI model utilized in implementing each method. Our evaluation revealed that a majority of studies employ synthetic data generators to (i) reduce the costs and duration linked to clinical trials for rare diseases, (ii) enhance the predictive performance of AI models in personalized medicine, and (iii) provide researchers with access to high-quality, representative multimodal datasets while protecting sensitive patient information, among other advantages. Synthetic data generators based on deep learning are both effective and appropriate for use in descriptive contexts as well as under constraints involving AI.

articleTitle: Using Machine Learning Techniques to Moderate CO2 Emission in KSA Future Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: As the world grapples with the escalating challenge of climate change, the role of innovative technologies in mitigating environmental impacts has never been more important. This study is inspired by the pioneering smart city of NEOM, Saudi Arabia; one of the forefronts of sustainable urban development, leveraging machine learning (ML) techniques to predict and mitigate carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions in the cities of Saudi Arabia. These cities are striving towards NEOM's approach to achieving zero emissions to the greatest extent possible, because NEOM needs the surrounding cities to have low CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission as well to achieve its goal. This research aims to create models based on machine learning that can precisely predict CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, utilizing a detailed dataset of vehicle emissions from Kaggle. We apply the following ML models: Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, Bagging, Backpropagation Neural Networks, Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The models are evaluated based on their Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) as well as Confusion Matrix in predicting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. Our analysis achieved the highest performance with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.99. Gradient Boosting and Bagging achieved the highest accuracies of 99%. Through a comprehensive review of recent studies and the application of diverse machine learning approaches, this proposed research identifies key challenges in reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions in smart cities, emphasizing the critical role of ML in enhancing the accuracy of forecasts across various sectors. Ultimately, that will support policy makers to make informed decisions to sustain a better urban development.

articleTitle: Vital Threat Detection and Monitoring Using Smartwatch and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The prevalence of chronic diseases and the increasing number of aging populations have created global demand for efficient health monitoring systems. While the current smartwatch technologies offer viable solutions, they encounter hard challenges like sensor integration, measurement accuracy, data privacy, and connectivity. This paper presents a novel smartwatch-based system, called Safepulse, that integrates multiple physiological sensors, employs machine learning for enhanced anomaly detection, and ensures data security by using advanced encryption. Using the adaptive architecture for reliable connectivity and the Six Sigma process optimization, Safepulse addresses these limitations to deliver accurate, real-time health monitoring and timely alerts. The system has been designed for the elderly and chronically ill patients and, therefore, facilitates improved health outcomes by enabling early detection and rapid medical intervention.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Accuracy of Multi-Table Potentials (MTPs) in Active Learning for Simulation and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: This study assesses the effectiveness of Multi-Table Potentials (MTPs) across various levels and evaluates the validity of a bottom-up training scheme using active learning. We performed active learning runs with MTP levels ranging from 6 to 14 and analyzed their performance in terms of training efficiency and predictive accuracy. The results indicate that the bottom-up approach is effective, as it achieves a comprehensive repre-sentation without requiring preselected configurations. Higher-level MTPs generally required fewer iterations but incurred higher computational costs. MTPs trained at later stages exhibited reduced training iteration counts with no improvement in validation performance compared to lower-level MTPs. Further analysis revealed that MTPs with higher levels while providing more accurate force and energy predictions, showed variability due to initial parameters. Specifically, lower-level MTPs demon-strated greater variance, especially in force predictions, which was minimized in higher-level models. The performance of MTPs in predicting elastic properties and radial distribution functions for solid and liquid potassium revealed that general-purpose MTPs struggled with precise property predictions, necessitating tailored training schemes or higher MTP levels for accuracy. Validation against practical datasets confirmed that MTPs of level 10 or higher generally provided better predictive accuracy, although challenges remain in ensuring stability and accuracy for specific configurations. The study recommends using MTP levels of at least 10 for general-purpose simulations and exploring higher levels for more precise applications.

articleTitle: Interpretable Arabic Hate Speech Detection using Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Social media platforms serve as significant spaces for users to have conversations, discussions and express their opinions. However, anonymity provided to users on these platforms allows the spread of hate speech and other offensive material. Due to the wide-ranging nature of these platforms, there is a critical need to automatically detect and report occurrences of hate speech. There are various detection methods, but many of them operate as black boxes, lacking interpretability and explainability by design. To address the lack of interpretability, this study explores the development of an interpretable framework to detect hate speech in Arabic using large language models (LLMs). The proposed approach combines advanced natural language processing techniques with interpretable machine learning methods to enhance understanding of model decisions. The experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves high accuracy while maintaining interpretability, enabling users to understand the reasoning behind the detections. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 0.846%, with a precision of 0.843% and a recall of 0.846%, outperforming existing Arabic hate speech detection models. These results show the effectiveness of combining LLM with interpretability for this critical task, providing a reliable and transparent solution for automated moderation of harmful content.

articleTitle: Advanced IoT-Enabled Forest Management System for Wildfire Detection and Ecosystem Protection: A Case Study in the Sundarbans
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Wildfires and deforestation are major threats to the Sundarbans ecosystem, driving biodiversity loss and escalating carbon emissions. This research proposes an innovative IoT-driven system for wildfire detection and ecosystem management, integrating Smart EcoHydrant Stations (SEHS), Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and blockchain technology. The proposed system utilizes a network of IoT-enabled sensors to monitor environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, smoke, CO2, methane, and air quality, while acoustic sensors detect fire sounds, distressed wildlife, and illegal logging activities. The SEHS system utilizes cameras to detect smoke and target areas at risk of fire spread with water, while UAVs deliver real-time thermal imaging data from hard-to-reach locations. LoRaWAN-based sensors enhance forest activity monitoring by identifying chainsaw noises and vibrations associated with illegal logging. In this system, solar energy and rechargeable batteries are used to ensure uninterrupted operation in remote areas, while satellite communication provides real-time alerts to forest authorities. This proposed system not only addresses wildfire detection but also combats deforestation, offering a robust, sustainable solution for preserving the Sundarbans' biodiversity and mitigating carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Battery Second-Life Performance Using Support Vector Regression and Voltage Features
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: Extensively used in electric vehicles (EVs), lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, undergo significant degradation after several charge-discharge cycles, leading to their retirement from high-demand applications. However, these batteries can still serve fewer demanding applications in their second life. Estimating the State of Health (SoH) in second-life applications is crucial for ensuring their reliable performance. This paper presents a method for SoH estimation using a Support Vector Regression (SVR) model trained in first-life battery data and applied to second-life usage. Two health indicators, TIECVD (Time Interval of Equal Charging Voltage Difference) and TIEDVD (Time Interval of Equal Discharging Voltage Difference) are extracted from voltage measurements and used as predictors in the SVR model. The method is validated using NASA's battery ageing dataset, consisting of three batteries (B0005, B0006, and B0007) with a rated capacity of 2 Ah. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 0.0061, 0.0158, and 0.0047 for the respective batteries during second life SoH estimation. This approach provides a practical, low-cost solution for estimating battery health in second-life applications without extensive monitoring systems.

articleTitle: A Federated Learning Approach to Strengthen IoT-Based Intrusion Detection Against Low-Rate DDoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Advanced Innovations in Smart Cities (ICAISC)
abstract: The rising cyber threats have made it necessary to enforce cybersecurity initiatives by organizations. Traditional approaches to intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are mostly centralized and therefore face substantial challenges like data privacy violations, high resource consumption and communication overhead. One promising solution to this issue is federated learning (FL), decentralized machine learning that can enable training models on edge devices to preserve data privacy. Further, FL, a global model is trained with multiple entities without sharing raw data so it can keep their privacy and communication costs are reduced. This is of great value above all in environments as IoT networks where importance of data sensitivity and privacy are crucial. FL achieves this without compromising much on scalability and resource efficiency compared to centralized approaches, which are two of their biggest limitations. Therefore, this paper discusses recent developments in FL for IDS and provides comprehensive analysis along with some initial results of FL in IoT-based intrusion detection. The proposed model achieves 99% accuracy in detecting low-rate DDoS attacks, which outperforms existing approaches.
